title: HER2-Low Biology and Determinants of Antibody-Drug Conjugate Payload Delivery in Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text:
Roughly half of all breast cancers classified as HER2-negative express HER2 protein at immunohistochemistry scores of 1+ or 2+ without gene amplification. This HER2-low population was long treated as biologically uninformative because trastuzumab and pertuzumab provide no benefit there. Trastuzumab deruxtecan changed that: an antibody-drug conjugate with a high drug-to-antibody ratio and a membrane-permeable topoisomerase I payload can produce durable responses at antigen densities far below the threshold for classical HER2-directed therapy. Why some HER2-low tumors respond and others do not is unknown. This U01 will quantify HER2 protein by mass spectrometry and immunofluorescence across 900 tumors, define the antigen density and internalization kinetics required for payload delivery in preclinical models, and dissect the bystander effect that allows killing of antigen-negative neighbors.

The problem is best stated as a mismatch between an assay and a question. The stain in routine use reports a four-level ordinal score whose thresholds were chosen so that amplified tumors separate cleanly from everything else, and it is deliberately configured so that weak signal is compressed toward the bottom of the scale. Asking that assay to distinguish 3,000 receptors per cell from 12,000 is asking it to resolve a range it was designed to collapse. Our preliminary data on 140 tumors show that the ordinal categories 0 and 1+ overlap substantially when the same specimens are measured on a continuous scale, and that the overlap region contains tumors that have responded to conjugate therapy.

The delivery question is separable from the abundance question and has been almost entirely neglected. A receptor that is abundant at the surface but recycles rather than trafficking to the lysosome will not deliver payload, and two tumors with identical staining may differ severalfold in the fraction of bound antibody that reaches an acidic compartment within the first hours. We have observed exactly this in a preliminary set of six models, where internalization rate varied 4.6-fold at matched surface abundance and correlated with intracellular payload better than abundance did. The same set showed a 2.3-fold spread in the fraction of internalized conjugate reaching an acidic compartment within 90 minutes, which is the step at which the linker is cleaved and the payload released.

The three aims are therefore arranged as a chain: how much antigen is present, how much of the bound conjugate is delivered, and how far the released payload reaches. Together they define the conditions under which a tumor with low antigen can nonetheless be killed, and they identify which of those conditions could be modified pharmacologically. All calibrated protein values, imaging data, and mixture-experiment results will be released with the archival cohort annotations in a form that permits independent re-estimation of the response threshold. The archival cohorts contributing to this work are already assembled, stained, and linked to treatment and outcome, so the project begins with specimen acquisition complete and proceeds directly to measurement.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text:
Our overall hypothesis is that response to a conjugate carrying a membrane-permeable payload is determined not by whether a tumor exceeds a staining category but by the product of three continuous quantities: antigen abundance, the rate at which bound conjugate reaches the lysosome, and the distance over which released payload remains cytotoxic. Each is measurable, each varies substantially among tumors that receive the same ordinal score, and each suggests a different way to extend the treatable population. The aims below measure the three quantities in the same experimental framework so that their relative contributions can be compared rather than asserted.

Aim 1 will establish an absolute HER2 protein scale using selected reaction monitoring mass spectrometry on 900 archival tumors, calibrated against quantitative immunofluorescence, and will determine where in that continuous scale response to trastuzumab deruxtecan begins. The 900 tumors span the full ordinal range including specimens scored 0, which is essential because a threshold cannot be located from a cohort truncated above it. Response data are available for an anticipated 210 conjugate-treated cases with central imaging review. The deliverable is a fitted relationship between protein abundance and best change in tumor diameter, with the location of any inflection reported as an interval rather than a point.

Aim 2 will measure receptor internalization and lysosomal trafficking rates in 22 preclinical models spanning two orders of magnitude of HER2 density, using pH-sensitive antibody labeling and live-cell imaging, and will relate these rates to intratumoral deruxtecan concentration measured by imaging mass spectrometry. Models are selected to include pairs matched on surface abundance but differing in trafficking, which permits the two variables to be separated experimentally rather than statistically. A secondary analysis will test whether agents that increase receptor turnover raise delivered payload at fixed surface abundance, which would define a pharmacologic route to extending eligibility.

Aim 3 will quantify the bystander effect by constructing defined mixtures of HER2-low and HER2-null cells and measuring killing of the null population as a function of mixing ratio, spatial arrangement in three-dimensional culture, and payload efflux through ABCC2 and ABCG2. The null population carries a distinguishable fluorescent label so that its survival can be measured directly rather than inferred from bulk viability. The primary parameter is an effective diffusion length, estimated from the decay of killing with distance in three-dimensional arrangements, and reported for cleavable and non-cleavable linker chemistries so that the contribution of linker design can be quantified.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text:
Immunohistochemistry was designed to identify amplified tumors and was never validated for discrimination within the low range. Concordance between pathologists for the distinction between a score of 0 and 1+ is only moderate, and this distinction now determines access to an effective drug. An absolute protein scale would replace an ordinal assay used outside its design range. Beyond assay reform, the biology matters: if response depends on internalization rate rather than surface density, then tumors with identical staining could differ predictably in benefit, and agents that increase receptor turnover could extend the eligible population. The bystander effect is equally consequential because it determines whether antigen heterogeneity within a tumor limits or is overcome by conjugate therapy.

The population affected by this measurement problem is large. Tumors expressing HER2 without amplification constitute a majority of hormone receptor-positive disease, so a boundary drawn in the wrong place, or drawn irreproducibly, misassigns tens of thousands of patients each year in the United States alone. Misassignment runs in both directions and the two errors are not symmetric in consequence: a patient denied an effective agent loses a treatment option outright, while a patient given it unnecessarily is exposed to pulmonary and hematologic risk without prospect of benefit. Neither error is currently measurable, because there is no reference method against which the ordinal call can be audited.

The trafficking hypothesis, if correct, changes what kind of test is needed. An abundance measurement, however well calibrated, cannot report how much of the bound conjugate reaches the compartment where the linker is cleaved. If two tumors with 10,000 receptors per cell differ fourfold in delivered payload because one recycles receptor and the other does not, then abundance will always be a lossy predictor and the residual variation will be misread as unexplained heterogeneity of response. Identifying trafficking as the limiting step would also nominate a class of intervention, since receptor internalization is modifiable by several agents already in clinical use for other purposes.

The bystander question determines how much intratumoral heterogeneity a conjugate can absorb. If released payload acts only on the cell that internalized the conjugate, then a tumor in which 30 percent of cells express antigen can lose at most 30 percent of its cells, and antigen-negative populations will be selected immediately. If the effective range extends tens of micrometers, heterogeneity is largely irrelevant and the relevant quantity becomes the spatial arrangement of expressing cells rather than their proportion. Measuring a diffusion length converts an argument that is currently conducted with cartoons into a number that can be compared between conjugates and used to predict which tumors will fail.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text:
We replace an ordinal stain with a calibrated protein measurement expressed in receptors per cell, a scale on which response thresholds can be estimated rather than assumed. We measure trafficking rather than inferring it, using ratiometric pH-sensitive conjugates that report the fraction of bound antibody that has reached the acidic lysosomal compartment within 90 minutes. We measure payload where it acts, by imaging mass spectrometry of tumor sections at 20-micron resolution, rather than in whole-tumor homogenate where stromal dilution obscures gradients. Finally, our defined-mixture platform makes the bystander effect a measured quantity with a diffusion length, which can then be compared across conjugates carrying cleavable and non-cleavable linkers.

Absolute quantification of a membrane protein in archival formalin-fixed tissue is not routine, and the reason is that peptide recovery from crosslinked material is variable. We address this with two proteotypic peptides whose recovery is tracked independently in every specimen using heavy-labeled internal standards added before digestion, so that a specimen with poor recovery is identified rather than reported as low-expressing. Agreement between the two peptides within a specimen is used as a per-sample quality metric, and specimens with more than twofold disagreement are re-extracted. This converts an assay that is usually run as a relative comparison into one that yields a number with a defensible uncertainty.

The ratiometric trafficking measurement is what allows internalization to be separated from binding. A conventional internalization assay reports the disappearance of surface signal, which conflates internalization with shedding and with dissociation. A pH-sensitive label that becomes fluorescent only in an acidic compartment, read against a pH-insensitive label on the same antibody, gives the fraction of bound molecules that have reached the lysosome as a ratio internal to each cell, which removes the dependence on how much antibody bound in the first place. Applied across 22 models at matched occupancy, it produces trafficking rates that can be compared directly with abundance as competing explanations.

Measuring payload in situ rather than in homogenate addresses a systematic error rather than a precision problem. Whole-tumor homogenate averages payload across malignant and stromal compartments and across regions that differ severalfold in perfusion, so a tumor with high local concentration in a well-perfused rim can report the same value as one with uniform low concentration. Imaging mass spectrometry at 20-micron resolution preserves the gradient, which is the quantity the bystander hypothesis is about. The principal limitation is sensitivity at the low end, and we accept that regions below the detection limit will be reported as censored rather than as zero.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text:
Archival blocks come from three institutional cohorts with linked treatment and outcome data. Selected reaction monitoring uses two proteotypic HER2 peptides with heavy-labeled internal standards, with a lower limit of quantification of 30 amol per microgram of protein. Immunofluorescence uses the 4B5 antibody with tyramide amplification and cell-line calibrators of known receptor number. Response thresholds are estimated by fitting a two-component mixture model to the continuous protein measurement against best percentage change in tumor diameter. Imaging mass spectrometry is performed on 12-micron cryosections with a matrix-assisted laser desorption source. Power calculations indicate that 900 tumors, with an anticipated 210 conjugate-treated cases, permit estimation of a response threshold with a 95 percent confidence interval width of approximately 0.4 log units.

Cohort assembly is prespecified to avoid the selection that has affected previous threshold estimates. Blocks are drawn consecutively within each institution from defined date ranges rather than from pathology archives searched for particular scores, and the ordinal score recorded at the time of clinical care is retained as a covariate but is not used for eligibility. Specimens are excluded only for insufficient tumor content or for fixation intervals outside a documented range, and the number excluded for each reason is reported. Calibrators of known receptor number are stained and quantified in every immunofluorescence batch, and batch-level calibration curves are fitted rather than assuming a single conversion across the study.

The analytic plan separates estimation of the abundance-response relationship from the question of whether a threshold exists at all. A monotone relationship without an inflection would indicate that the drug's activity declines smoothly with abundance and that any cutoff is arbitrary, which is a different conclusion from a genuine threshold and demands a different clinical response. We therefore fit both a smooth monotone model and a two-component mixture and compare them by cross-validated predictive performance, reporting the comparison rather than presenting only the model that fits best. Trafficking and abundance are entered jointly in a model of intratumoral payload so that their partial contributions can be estimated, with model identity as a random effect.

Anticipated difficulties are threefold. If peptide recovery from older blocks proves unacceptable, the analysis will be restricted to a prespecified window of fixation year, with the excluded fraction reported and the threshold estimate repeated in the restricted set. If the conjugate-treated subset falls below 150 cases, the threshold interval will widen beyond the target and we will pool with a partner cohort under a prespecified harmonization protocol that includes exchange of calibrators. If the bystander effect proves too short-range to measure reliably in three-dimensional culture, the mixture experiments will be repeated in xenografts constructed from labeled populations, which sacrifices control over arrangement but preserves the biological question. Rigor is supported by blinding of all quantitative measurements to treatment and outcome, by prespecification of the analysis plan before any outcome data are linked, and by release of raw spectra and image data at publication.

title: Overcoming PI3K Pathway-Mediated Resistance After CDK4/6 Inhibition in ER-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text:
Activating PIK3CA mutations are present in about 40 percent of hormone receptor-positive breast cancers and are enriched further in tumors that have progressed on CDK4/6 inhibitors. Alpelisib with fulvestrant improves progression-free survival in this population, but median benefit is short, roughly 11 months in the registration trial and closer to 7 months after CDK4/6 exposure, and hyperglycemia and rash force dose reduction or interruption in a third of patients. The pathway is therefore validated but poorly exploited. This project asks why the PI3K pathway becomes dominant after CDK4/6 blockade, whether AKT-directed rather than alpha-isoform-directed inhibition is better suited to that setting, and how the metabolic consequences of alpha-isoform inhibition can be blunted so that effective exposure is sustained.

The three questions are linked by a single observation from our preliminary work. In 22 paired biopsies taken before treatment and at progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor, phosphorylation of AKT at serine 473 rose by a median of 2.4-fold, and the rise was present in tumors with and without a PIK3CA mutation. Pathway output at the moment of clinical decision-making is therefore not predicted by the genotype determined at diagnosis, which is the only genotype most patients have. This is the observation that makes a paired-biopsy design necessary and that motivates comparing agents acting at different nodes of the pathway rather than assuming that genotype dictates the node.

The metabolic component follows from the pharmacology of alpha-isoform inhibition rather than from any tumor-intrinsic property. Blocking p110-alpha in insulin-responsive tissues raises blood glucose within days, the pancreas responds with insulin, and insulin acts on the tumor through the same receptor tyrosine kinases the drug was intended to interrupt. Every element of that loop is measurable, and in tumor-bearing mice we have shown that suppressing the insulin response restores tumor phospho-AKT suppression at unchanged drug exposure. Whether the same holds in patients is the question the embedded pilot addresses. We have measured each element of the loop in tumor-bearing animals, and the tumor consequence is reversible within 48 hours of restoring glucose control, which is what makes it a target rather than merely a correlate.

Expected deliverables are a description of how pathway output changes under CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure in paired human tissue, a head-to-head comparison of three pathway-directed agents in models stratified by genotype, and a first clinical estimate of whether a metabolic intervention reduces the dose interruptions that currently truncate exposure. Phosphoproteomic data, model growth curves, and the clinical pilot's glucose and insulin time series will be deposited in public repositories. The paired biopsy resource, the ten characterized xenografts, and the clinical pilot infrastructure are all in place, so the project's principal risk lies in the biology rather than in the assembly of materials. Each aim yields an interpretable result whether the hypothesis is supported or not.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text:
The central premise is that the PI3K pathway is not simply present in these tumors but becomes functionally dominant during CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure, and that the failure of alpha-isoform inhibition to deliver more than a few months of benefit reflects two separate problems: the node targeted may not be the node that matters after CDK4/6 blockade, and the exposure achieved is truncated by a metabolic feedback that the drug itself creates. The three aims address the pathway state, the choice of node, and the feedback. Each aim is powered independently, and the three are linked through a shared cohort and a shared set of models so that a pathway state observed in patients can be interrogated pharmacologically in a system that carries the same genotype.

Aim 1 will define how PI3K pathway output changes during CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, using reverse-phase protein arrays and phosphoproteomics on 60 paired biopsies to quantify AKT serine 473, PRAS40, S6 ribosomal protein, and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation before treatment and at progression. Each pair is analyzed on the same plate and in the same mass spectrometry batch, with the baseline and progression specimens randomized within batch so that a systematic pre-post difference cannot arise from run order. The prespecified primary contrast is the within-patient change in AKT serine 473 phosphorylation, tested by paired analysis and reported separately for PIK3CA-mutant and wild-type tumors.

Aim 2 will compare alpelisib, capivasertib, and everolimus in ten patient-derived xenografts stratified by PIK3CA and AKT1 genotype, each combined with fulvestrant, with tumor growth delay and duration of control as endpoints. All three agents are tested concurrently in the same models with a shared fulvestrant control arm, which is what makes the comparison interpretable; each was originally developed against a different comparator, so no existing dataset supports a direct ranking. Models include four derived from patients with documented progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Duration of control is defined prospectively as time to a doubling of nadir volume.

Aim 3 will test whether a ketogenic diet or an SGLT2 inhibitor prevents the insulin feedback that limits alpha-isoform inhibition, measuring glucose, insulin, and tumor phospho-AKT in tumor-bearing mice and in a 40-patient pilot embedded in NCT04073680. The preclinical component establishes whether suppressing the insulin response restores pathway suppression in tumor; the clinical component asks the narrower and more immediate question of whether the intervention keeps patients on drug. The clinical primary endpoint is the proportion requiring dose interruption for hyperglycemia, with serial glucose, insulin, and C-peptide collected to confirm that the intended metabolic effect was achieved.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text:
Endocrine resistance after CDK4/6 inhibition is now the commonest clinical scenario in hormone receptor-positive metastatic disease, and PI3K pathway activation is its commonest tractable driver. Yet alpha-isoform inhibition is self-limiting: blocking p110-alpha in muscle and liver raises blood glucose, the resulting insulin surge reactivates the pathway in tumor, and dose interruption for hyperglycemia occurs in 20 to 30 percent of treated patients. This is a pharmacologic problem with a metabolic solution, and preclinical work suggests that suppressing the insulin response restores drug effect. Establishing which patients should receive alpha-isoform versus AKT-directed inhibition, and how to keep them on treatment, would extend a benefit that currently lasts months.

The scale of the affected population is what makes a few months of additional benefit worth pursuing. Nearly every patient with hormone receptor-positive metastatic disease now receives a CDK4/6 inhibitor in the first line, and roughly 40 percent of them carry an activating PIK3CA mutation, so the post-CDK4/6 pathway-directed decision is faced tens of thousands of times each year. The alternative at that decision point is usually chemotherapy, which has its own toxicity profile and no better duration of control, so improvements in the tolerability and duration of the targeted option translate directly into deferred chemotherapy.

The choice between nodes is currently made by genotype alone, and there is reason to doubt that this is right. Alpha-isoform inhibition presupposes that signaling flows through p110-alpha, which is a reasonable inference in a PIK3CA-mutant tumor at diagnosis but not necessarily after months of selective pressure from a different drug class. AKT-directed inhibition acts downstream of any upstream input, including insulin, and would be expected to be less vulnerable to the feedback loop that limits the alpha-selective agent, but at the cost of blocking a node with broader physiologic roles. No dataset compares them where the decision is actually made.

Finally, treating hyperglycemia as a mechanism of failure rather than an adverse event reframes what supportive care is for. Under the current framing, glucose is managed to keep the patient safe and the tumor is not considered; under the proposed framing, glucose is managed because insulin is reactivating the target and the tumor consequence is measurable. If the reframing is correct, the same intervention improves both tolerability and efficacy, and the improvement can be verified in tissue rather than inferred from progression-free survival alone. It also creates a measurable intermediate endpoint for early-phase development, since a regimen that restores pathway suppression in a serial biopsy has demonstrated its intended mechanism long before any progression-free survival curve can separate.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text:
Rather than treating hyperglycemia as a nuisance to be managed after the fact, we treat it as a mechanism of drug failure to be prevented in advance, and we measure the tumor consequence directly through phospho-AKT in serial biopsies rather than inferring it from glucose alone. We also compare three pathway agents head to head in the post-CDK4/6 setting, a comparison that has never been made because each was developed against a different control. Our paired-biopsy design captures the pathway state at the moment of clinical decision-making rather than at diagnosis, which is when the pathway state is currently measured and when it is least informative.

The measurement strategy is the enabling advance. Phosphorylation states are labile, and the usual reason that pre-post comparisons in human tissue are uninformative is that the ischemic interval between acquisition and freezing varies between specimens by more than the biological effect being measured. Our protocol fixes the interval at under 3 minutes with a stabilizing reagent applied at the bedside, records it for every specimen, and includes it as a covariate. This is unglamorous but it is the difference between a phosphoproteomic dataset that reports biology and one that reports specimen handling. We report the interval for every specimen and exclude none on that basis, so that readers can judge for themselves whether handling could account for any reported difference.

The three-agent comparison is designed to answer a question the development pathway systematically avoids. Sponsors compare their agent against a control that makes approval likely, not against the agent a clinician would otherwise choose, so the literature accumulates as a set of non-overlapping comparisons. Running all three in the same models, on the same schedule, with a shared control arm and prespecified endpoints, produces a ranking with an uncertainty estimate. We recognize that model-based rankings do not always transfer to patients, and we therefore report the comparison alongside genotype-stratified subgroup estimates rather than as a single verdict.

The dietary and pharmacologic arms of the metabolic aim were chosen to test the mechanism from two directions. A ketogenic formulation lowers the substrate that drives the insulin response; an SGLT2 inhibitor increases urinary glucose loss without acting on insulin secretion directly. If both restore tumor pathway suppression, the mechanism is insulin rather than any idiosyncratic property of the intervention. If only one does, the discrepancy itself is informative. The principal risk is that neither is tolerable alongside the drug in patients, and the pilot is powered and monitored to detect that early. We therefore specify stopping rules based on weight loss and on ketone concentrations rather than on investigator judgment, and the pilot is designed so that failure of one intervention does not compromise evaluation of the other.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text:
Paired biopsies come from an existing registry with 71 percent progression-biopsy capture. Phosphoproteomics uses tandem mass tag labeling with titanium dioxide enrichment, quantifying approximately 9,000 phosphosites per sample. Xenografts are treated for 60 days or until tumors reach 1,500 cubic millimeters. Mice receive alpelisib 35 mg/kg daily, capivasertib 100 mg/kg on a four-days-on schedule, or everolimus 5 mg/kg daily. The dietary aim uses a 4:1 ketogenic formulation and dapagliflozin at 1 mg/kg. In the clinical pilot, 40 patients provide 80 percent power to detect a reduction in the proportion requiring dose interruption for hyperglycemia from 30 percent to 8 percent using an exact binomial test at one-sided alpha of 0.10.

Specimen and batch design deserve explicit description because the primary comparison is a within-patient difference. Each tandem mass tag set contains both members of five or six patient pairs plus a common reference channel constructed from a pooled lysate, so that ratios are computed within set and normalized across sets through the reference. Sets are balanced for baseline and progression specimens and for treatment received. Reverse-phase protein array measurements are made on the same lysates and used as an orthogonal confirmation for the four prespecified phosphosites, with agreement between platforms reported as a concordance correlation coefficient rather than assumed.

The statistical plan for the preclinical comparison treats model as the unit of replication. Tumor volume trajectories are log-transformed and fitted in a mixed-effects framework with model identity as a random intercept and agent as a fixed effect, with fulvestrant alone as the reference. Pairwise contrasts among the three agents are prespecified and adjusted for multiplicity by a step-down procedure. In the clinical pilot, the primary analysis is an exact binomial comparison against the 30 percent historical rate, with a prespecified interim safety review after 15 patients; serial glucose, insulin, and C-peptide are analyzed as area under the curve over the first 8 weeks and related to whether interruption occurred.

Several contingencies are planned for. If fewer than 60 usable pairs accrue within the projected interval, the phosphoproteomic aim will be completed at 45 pairs, which preserves 80 percent power for a within-patient change of 1.8-fold at the observed variance, and the reduction will be reported rather than absorbed. If the ketogenic formulation proves unacceptable in the clinical pilot, accrual will continue on the SGLT2 arm alone under a prespecified adaptation rule. If capivasertib produces intolerable weight loss in the xenograft experiments at the planned schedule, the schedule will be reduced to a three-days-on cycle with exposure confirmed by terminal plasma sampling, and the change will be applied to all models rather than to those responding poorly. Rigor is supported by randomization of animals by cage after stratification on tumor volume, blinded caliper measurement, blinded central review of glucose events in the clinical pilot, and prespecified statistical analysis plans filed before unblinding.

title: Therapy-Induced Senescence as a Determinant of CDK4/6 Inhibitor Durability

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text:
Palbociclib, ribociclib, and abemaciclib are cytostatic in most hormone receptor-positive breast cancer cells: they impose a durable arrest rather than killing. A large fraction of arrested cells acquire the flattened morphology, beta-galactosidase activity, lysosomal expansion, and inflammatory secretory phenotype of senescence. Senescent tumor cells are not inert. They persist for months, they secrete interleukin 6 and CXCL8, and a fraction of them re-enter proliferation when drug is withdrawn, seeding regrowth. We propose that the durability of CDK4/6 inhibition is set by the balance between how many cells enter this state, how long they remain in it, and how efficiently they are cleared by immune surveillance. This project will quantify that balance and test whether pharmacologic clearance of senescent cells converts a cytostatic response into a lasting one.

The proposal rests on a distinction that is easy to state and has rarely been tested. Deepening an arrest and eliminating arrested cells are different objectives requiring different drugs, and almost all combination development in this disease has pursued the first. If the reservoir of arrested cells is the source of regrowth, then adding a second antiproliferative agent acts on the population that is already controlled and leaves the population that matters untouched. Our preliminary data show that the arrested fraction reaches 61 percent by day 21 in three xenografts and remains above half at day 60, while tumor volume is unchanged, which is exactly the configuration in which the distinction becomes practically important.

Escape from the state is measurable and is not rare. Using a fluorescent reporter of lysosomal beta-galactosidase activity together with a proliferation label, we have observed that a small percentage of cells that acquired the reporter signal subsequently divided, and that the frequency of such events rises sharply after drug withdrawal. This is the observation that connects the persistent population to clinical regrowth, and it is the reason we treat entry, persistence, and escape as three separately estimable rates rather than as a single categorical state. Because escape events are individually rare but collectively decisive for regrowth, estimating their frequency requires following many cells over weeks rather than scoring a population once, which is the design constraint that shapes the first aim.

We expect to deliver rate estimates for entry, persistence, and escape in patient-derived systems; a genetic map of the survival dependencies of arrested cells generated in cells that are already arrested rather than cycling; and a test of whether intermittent pharmacologic clearance prolongs disease control, with the immune contribution to that effect separated by depletion rather than by inference. Imaging, screen, and growth data will be released in full, and the reporter models will be distributed to other laboratories. The reagents required are in hand: the reporter models are established and characterized, the focused library is constructed, and the senolytic agents are commercially available at research grade, so the project begins with execution rather than with development.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text:
The hypothesis is that the durability of CDK4/6 inhibition is governed by three separable quantities: the fraction of cells that enter a persistent arrested state, the length of time they remain in it, and the rate at which they are removed, whether pharmacologically or by the host. Existing work reports the first as a percentage at a single time point and does not measure the other two at all. The aims below estimate all three, identify what keeps the arrested cells alive, and test whether removing them changes the outcome. Each aim is designed to yield an interpretable answer independently, but the value of the set lies in their sequence, since the schedule tested in the third aim is derived from the entry kinetics measured in the first.

Aim 1 will quantify the senescent fraction and its persistence during continuous palbociclib exposure in twelve patient-derived xenografts and six organoid lines, using a lysosomal beta-galactosidase reporter, p16 and p21 immunostaining, and an eighteen-gene secretory signature. Serial intravital imaging of the same tumor at days 0, 7, 14, 21, 42, and 60 yields entry and persistence as fitted rates rather than as differences between independent cohorts. A prespecified secondary analysis will relate the entry rate to baseline RB1 protein and to the eleven-transcript proliferative output, testing whether models that arrest efficiently are those with the most intact pathway. The deliverable is a rate table across eighteen models.

Aim 2 will define the survival dependencies of the senescent population by CRISPR screening in arrested cells, with validation of BCL-xL, BCL-2, and MCL1 dependence using navitoclax, venetoclax, and A-1331852. The screen is introduced after 14 days of arrest so that the dependencies measured are those of the arrested state rather than of the cycling population from which it arose, and library representation is maintained without requiring proliferation by using a non-expanding dropout design with matched input controls. Hits are validated genetically by two independent guides and pharmacologically by agents with distinct selectivity profiles, and cross-validated in three organoid lines.

Aim 3 will test whether intermittent senolytic exposure after 21 days of palbociclib prolongs the interval to tumor regrowth relative to continuous palbociclib alone, and will determine whether natural killer cell depletion abolishes any benefit, thereby distinguishing direct clearance from immune-mediated clearance. The 21-day delay is chosen from the entry kinetics in Aim 1 so that the intervention is applied when the target population exists. Regrowth is defined prospectively as a doubling of nadir volume. The depletion arm is the mechanistic control that determines whether the agent is acting on the tumor cell or on its visibility to the host.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text:
The clinical behavior of CDK4/6 inhibitors is unusual: responses are shallow but prolonged, and disease often regrows quickly once the drug is stopped. Both observations are consistent with a large persistent arrested population rather than with tumor cell elimination. If that population is the reservoir from which the disease returns, then eliminating it is a distinct therapeutic goal from deepening the initial arrest, and it requires different drugs. Senolytic agents are already in human testing for age-related indications, so the translational path is short. Establishing that the arrested reservoir governs durability would reframe combination strategy away from adding a second antiproliferative agent and toward clearing cells that have already stopped dividing.

The strategic consequence is immediate because the field's current combination pipeline is almost entirely antiproliferative. Agents directed at the kinases, at the receptor, and at the pathways feeding both share a mechanism of action that acts on cells attempting to divide. If the limiting population is not attempting to divide, then these combinations are being evaluated against the wrong target, and the modest incremental benefits observed are consistent with that interpretation. Redirecting even a fraction of that development effort toward clearance would be a substantial reallocation, and it should be justified by direct measurement rather than by analogy to other diseases.

The secretory program adds a second reason to care about the reservoir beyond its role as a source of regrowth. Cells in this state release mediators that act on fibroblasts, endothelium, and leukocytes, so a large persistent population is not merely inert mass but an active modifier of the tissue around it. Whether that modification is favorable or unfavorable over months of continuous drug exposure is unknown and is likely to differ between the early and late phases of treatment. Any account of durability that ignores this is incomplete, though our own design can address it only partially.

Finally, the question has an unusually short translational path. Agents that selectively kill cells in this state exist, have been dosed in humans, and have characterized toxicity profiles, and one of the principal liabilities of the first-generation compound is addressed by a more selective successor. A convincing preclinical demonstration that clearance prolongs control would therefore lead to a testable clinical regimen rather than to a discovery program, which is not usually true of mechanistic findings in this disease. It would also give the field a well-defined pharmacodynamic endpoint, since clearance of the target population can in principle be measured in serial tissue rather than inferred from tumor volume alone.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text:
Existing work infers senescence from staining at a single time point in cell lines. We follow the state longitudinally in vivo using a knock-in beta-galactosidase reporter that permits serial intravital imaging of the same tumor, so that entry, persistence, and escape can be measured as rates rather than snapshots. Our CRISPR screen is performed in cells that have already been arrested for 14 days, which is essential because the survival dependencies of arrested cells differ substantially from those of cycling cells. Finally, we test the immune contribution by depletion rather than by correlation, which distinguishes a drug acting on the tumor cell from a drug acting by exposing it to natural killer cells.

Longitudinal in vivo measurement solves a problem that cross-sectional designs cannot. A histochemical stain applied to independent cohorts at successive time points gives a sequence of prevalences, and prevalence is a function of both entry and exit; a stable prevalence is equally consistent with a static population and with rapid turnover. Following the same tumor over time, with a reporter whose signal is acquired and can be lost, allows entry and exit to be estimated separately. This distinction determines whether a clearance strategy needs to be applied once or repeatedly, which is a design question for any eventual trial.

Screening in an arrested population is technically awkward and is the reason it is seldom done. Dropout screens depend on proliferation to deplete guides targeting essential genes, and a population that does not divide provides no such amplification. We use a design in which the readout is survival of the arrested population over an extended interval against a matched input, with representation maintained by starting at 500-fold coverage and sequencing deeply enough to detect twofold depletion. The trade-off is reduced sensitivity for weak dependencies, which we accept because the hypothesis concerns strong, targetable ones. The design also requires a matched input control harvested at the moment the library is introduced, which we obtain by splitting the arrested population rather than by relying on a plasmid reference.

Testing the immune contribution by depletion rather than by correlation is a small methodological point with a large interpretive consequence. If a senolytic extends control and the effect disappears when a lymphocyte population is removed, the agent is acting at least in part by rendering cells visible rather than by killing them outright, and the clinical implication is that it should be combined with agents that support that population rather than with further cytotoxic pressure. Correlative immune profiling cannot distinguish these, and the distinction determines the next combination. The experiment is also cheap to run alongside the efficacy comparison, since the depletion antibody is administered to a parallel arm of the same study rather than in a separate protocol.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text:
Xenografts are established in NSG mice and, for immune experiments, matched syngeneic lines are used in immunocompetent BALB/c hosts. Palbociclib is given at 90 mg/kg daily. Navitoclax is administered at 50 mg/kg on a two-days-per-week intermittent schedule beginning at day 21. The secretory signature is measured by NanoString on laser-captured tumor regions. CRISPR screening uses a 4,000-guide library targeting apoptotic regulators at 500-fold representation. Regrowth is defined as the time from treatment start to a doubling of the nadir tumor volume. Twelve models with eight mice per arm provide 85 percent power to detect a 45 percent extension in time to regrowth, analyzed by mixed-effects Cox regression with model as a random effect.

Intravital imaging is performed through a dorsal window or a mammary imaging window depending on implantation site, with the same field registered across sessions using implanted fiducial marks. Reporter signal is quantified per cell after segmentation, and a cell is classified as reporter-positive above a threshold set from untreated tumors imaged in the same session. Because photobleaching and window-related inflammation both accumulate with repeated imaging, each animal contributes a maximum of six sessions and a subset of animals is imaged on an offset schedule so that any session-number artifact can be detected. Histochemical and immunostaining measurements are made on terminal tissue from parallel animals as an orthogonal confirmation of the reporter readout.

The analytic plan estimates entry and exit rates from the imaging data using a two-state model in which cells transition between reporter-negative and reporter-positive compartments, fitted per model with hierarchical pooling across models. Growth and regrowth analyses use mixed-effects Cox regression with model identity as a random effect, and the senolytic effect is estimated as a hazard ratio for regrowth with the depletion arm entered as an interaction term. Screen data are analyzed by comparing guide abundance in the surviving arrested population against matched input, with false discovery control at 5 percent and a prespecified requirement that a hit be supported by at least three of six guides.

Three risks require contingency planning. If the reporter alters the behavior of the state it reports, which we will test by comparing reporter-bearing and parental lines for arrest fraction and regrowth kinetics, the imaging aim will be repeated with a second reporter integrated at a different locus. If the arrested population proves too fragile for library-scale manipulation, the screen will be replaced by an arrayed test of a 200-gene focused set, which sacrifices discovery breadth but preserves the validation logic. If natural killer depletion is incomplete, confirmed by flow cytometry in every experiment, animals below a prespecified depletion threshold are excluded before unblinding. All experiments are randomized by cage after stratification on tumor volume, measurements are made blinded to arm, and sample sizes are fixed in advance with attrition reported.

title: Circulating Tumor DNA-Guided Adaptive Endocrine Therapy and Molecular Residual Disease

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text:
Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer relapses late; half of all distant recurrences occur more than five years after surgery, and current tools cannot identify which women carry residual disease during that interval. In the metastatic setting the same technology problem appears in a different form: treatment is changed only when imaging changes, months after the tumor has already escaped. This U01 applies tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA assays to both settings. We will determine the sensitivity and lead time of molecular residual disease detection after adjuvant endocrine therapy in 1,100 women, characterize the emergence of ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations and other escape lesions in plasma, and conduct a randomized trial, NCT04567420, testing whether escalating therapy at molecular relapse rather than at radiographic relapse improves distant relapse-free survival.

The two settings share an assay problem and differ in what is at stake. After surgery the quantity of tumor DNA in circulation is minute, often below one mutant molecule per milliliter, so detection depends on tracking many patient-specific variants simultaneously rather than on depth at any single locus. In advanced disease the burden is higher and the analytic challenge is instead one of interpretation: distinguishing a rise that signals escape from the fluctuation that occurs during stable disease. Our preliminary work in 180 women establishes both the analytic floor for the adjuvant assay and the magnitude of on-treatment variation in the advanced setting.

Preliminary results support the feasibility of the residual disease aim. Among 180 women sampled at 6-month intervals after surgery, detection preceded clinical relapse in 34 of 38 relapsing patients, with a median interval of 10.4 months and a maximum of 33 months, and 2 of 142 non-relapsing women had a single positive draw that did not repeat on subsequent sampling. These figures inform both the confirmation rule adopted for the randomized aim and the assumed event rate in the escalation arm. The two non-relapsing women with an isolated positive draw are also informative, since they define the failure mode that a confirmation requirement is designed to eliminate and they set an upper bound on the rate at which escalation would be offered unnecessarily.

We expect to deliver performance characteristics for a personalized assay in the setting where it would be used, a description of the plasma profile at the moment of molecular relapse, and a randomized estimate of whether escalating therapy at that moment changes distant relapse-free survival. The sample bank, the personalized variant panels, and the linked clinical data will be maintained as a resource beyond the project period, and all assay performance data will be published irrespective of the trial's outcome. The infrastructure required is largely in place: the sampling network, the central laboratory, and the panel design pipeline have all been operating for three years, so the project's risk lies in accrual and retention rather than in assay development.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text:
The premise is that both the adjuvant and the advanced settings are limited by the same thing: a decision that must wait for an anatomic change that occurs long after the biological one. The aims establish how much earlier the biological change can be detected, what it looks like when detected, and whether acting on it earlier improves outcome. The first two aims are observational and support the third, which is the aim that determines whether the technology becomes a management tool or remains a prognostic curiosity. The three aims draw on a single cohort and a single laboratory workflow, which means that the performance characteristics estimated in the first aim apply directly to the assay used to select participants for the third.

Aim 1 will establish analytic and clinical performance of a personalized 48-variant assay for molecular residual disease in 1,100 women completing surgery and adjuvant endocrine therapy, sampled every 6 months for 6 years, with sensitivity, specificity, and lead time relative to imaging as endpoints. Sensitivity is estimated among women who subsequently relapse and is reported both per-draw and per-patient across the full sampling series; specificity is estimated among women remaining relapse-free at 6 years, which requires the full follow-up interval and is the reason the aim is not shorter. Analytic performance is characterized separately using contrived dilutions spanning 0.005 to 0.1 percent, run in the same laboratory workflow as the clinical specimens.

Aim 2 will characterize the plasma genomic profile at molecular relapse, focusing on ESR1 ligand-binding domain substitutions, PIK3CA mutations, and RB1 loss, and will determine which of these are detectable before any radiographic abnormality. This aim uses broader sequencing applied to the draw at which the personalized assay first turns positive and to the two subsequent draws, so that the composition of the emerging population can be described rather than merely its existence. A prespecified analysis will ask whether the alterations present at molecular relapse differ from those in the resected primary, which addresses whether escalation should be directed by the archival specimen or by the plasma.

Aim 3 will randomize 620 women with detectable molecular residual disease to continued standard adjuvant endocrine therapy or to escalation with fulvestrant plus ribociclib, with distant relapse-free survival as the primary endpoint and a planned interim analysis after 90 events. Randomization occurs after a confirmed positive result on two draws, which limits the number of women escalated on the basis of a single unreproducible signal. Quality of life and treatment discontinuation are collected as key secondary endpoints, since escalation imposes real toxicity on women who are, by every conventional measure, disease-free at the time of assignment.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text:
Adjuvant endocrine therapy is given to nearly every woman with hormone receptor-positive disease, most of whom are already cured and none of whom can be identified. Extended therapy to ten years yields an absolute benefit of about 3 percent while imposing years of symptoms on the other 97 percent. A test that identifies residual disease would allow escalation for the few and de-escalation for the many. In advanced disease, waiting for imaging change means that a switch of therapy is always made against a larger, more heterogeneous tumor burden than necessary. The value of acting earlier is plausible but unproven, and the only way to establish it is a randomized comparison rather than another observational lead-time study.

The late-relapse pattern of this disease is what makes the problem both important and hard. Recurrences continue at a roughly constant annual rate for at least two decades after surgery, so a woman who is well at year five has not been reassured about years six through twenty. No imaging strategy has been shown to help, because scanning a population with a low annual event rate produces mostly false positives and finds true events at a size where treatment intent does not change. A blood-based test with a long lead time is the only approach that addresses the interval where the events actually occur.

The de-escalation half of the argument deserves as much emphasis as the escalation half, though it is harder to test. Years of endocrine therapy impose joint symptoms, vasomotor symptoms, bone loss, and sexual dysfunction on a population that is overwhelmingly cured, and a substantial fraction stop early as a result. A test with high negative predictive value across repeated sampling would permit shorter treatment for the women who need none, which would improve quality of life for far more people than escalation would help. Establishing the negative predictive value is a prerequisite, and it requires the full six-year follow-up this aim provides.

The randomized component addresses the objection that would otherwise be fatal. Every observational report of a lead time invites the inference that acting earlier must be better, but earlier detection changes the measured interval to relapse whether or not it changes the outcome, and the patients whose tests turn positive differ systematically from those whose do not. Only randomization among the test-positive group can establish that escalation helps, and only a control arm receiving current standard therapy makes a positive result immediately actionable. It also means that a negative result is interpretable, since it would establish that the lead time provided by the test does not translate into benefit when the escalation offered is the one currently available.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text:
Most residual disease studies sample once or twice and report a hazard ratio. We sample every 6 months for 6 years, which permits estimation of the interval between first detection and clinical relapse for each individual and turns a prognostic association into an actionable window. Our assay is personalized to each tumor and tracks 48 variants rather than a fixed gene panel, giving detection at 0.008 percent variant allele fraction, roughly an order of magnitude better than off-the-shelf panels. The randomized escalation aim is designed so that the control arm receives the current standard, meaning that a positive result changes practice immediately rather than requiring a further confirmatory trial.

Tracking many variants rather than achieving extreme depth at few is the analytic idea that makes detection at this level possible. The limit on sensitivity in a plasma sample is not read depth but the number of genome equivalents present, which is fixed by the volume drawn; once every informative molecule has been sequenced, further depth adds nothing. Distributing the search across 48 loci multiplies the number of informative molecules by 48 without requiring more blood, and it converts the detection problem from a single-locus call to an aggregate test with a calculable false-positive rate. The cost is that a personalized panel must be designed and manufactured for every patient.

The six-year sampling schedule is unusual and expensive, and it is justified by the disease rather than by preference. Studies that sample for two years capture only the early recurrences, which are the minority in this subtype and are biologically distinct from late ones. A per-patient lead time can only be estimated for patients whose relapse is observed within the sampling window, so a short window yields lead-time estimates that are biased toward the early-relapsing subset. Sampling through the interval where most events occur is the only way to describe the behavior of the test where it would actually be used.

Designing the randomized aim against current standard therapy rather than against observation is a deliberate constraint that costs statistical power and buys immediate interpretability. A comparison against observation would show a larger difference and would be easier to complete, but it would not answer the question a clinician faces, which is whether to add something to what she is already giving. The principal risk of this design is that the control arm performs better than assumed, which we address through a prespecified interim analysis and through an event-driven rather than time-driven final analysis. The design also fixes the escalation regimen rather than leaving it to investigator choice, which sacrifices flexibility but ensures that a positive result names a specific strategy that can be adopted without further interpretation.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text:
Whole-exome sequencing of the primary tumor identifies 48 patient-specific somatic variants, which are then tracked in 20 mL of plasma by multiplex PCR followed by deep sequencing at 100,000-fold read depth per amplicon. Detection requires two or more variants above background with a Monte Carlo p value below 0.001. Lead time is estimated by interval-censored survival methods. For the randomized aim, 620 participants with an expected 3-year distant relapse-free survival of 62 percent in the control arm provide 84 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.65 at a two-sided alpha of 0.05, with stratification by nodal status, prior chemotherapy, and time since surgery.

Variant selection for each personalized panel follows a fixed algorithm rather than manual curation, which is what makes the assay reproducible across 1,100 patients. Candidate variants are ranked by clonality inferred from copy-number-corrected allele fraction, filtered to remove those in regions of copy-number loss, in homopolymer contexts, or overlapping known common polymorphisms, and the top 48 are selected. Variants also detected in matched leukocyte DNA are excluded before panel design, which removes clonal hematopoietic signal at the design stage rather than at the analysis stage. Every batch includes a contrived positive at 0.01 percent and eight negative controls, and the background error model is refitted from the negatives in each batch.

The analysis plan addresses three distinct estimands. Per-patient sensitivity is estimated among relapsing women as the proportion with at least one confirmed positive draw before clinical relapse, with confidence intervals from the exact binomial. Lead time is estimated by interval-censored methods that account for the fact that the true onset lies between the last negative and the first positive draw, which a naive analysis using the positive draw date would systematically understate. The randomized comparison uses a stratified Cox model with a single prespecified interim analysis at 90 events using an O'Brien-Fleming boundary, and the primary analysis is by intention to treat with a prespecified per-protocol sensitivity analysis.

The principal risks are accrual to the randomized aim, the confirmed-positive rate, and long-term retention. If fewer than the projected number of women test positive, the randomized aim will extend accrual through additional network sites rather than relax the confirmation requirement, since a single-draw trigger would enroll women whose signal does not reproduce and would dilute the estimate. If retention across six years falls below 80 percent, we will report performance with inverse-probability-of-censoring weights and will describe the characteristics of those lost. If the escalation regimen proves poorly tolerated in a population that feels well, discontinuation will be reported as a co-primary practical outcome rather than as a footnote. Rigor is supported by central blinded review of relapse events, by laboratory staff blinded to clinical status, and by a data and safety monitoring board with prespecified stopping guidance.

title: Immune Consequences of CDK4/6 Blockade in Estrogen Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text:
CDK4 and CDK6 are not restricted to tumor cells. Their inhibition alters antigen presentation, derepresses endogenous retroviral transcripts, suppresses regulatory T cell proliferation more than that of effector T cells, and induces a durable arrest accompanied by an inflammatory secretory program that recruits myeloid and lymphoid populations into the tumor bed. These observations suggest that a drug developed as an antiproliferative agent is also an immune modulator, and that combining it with checkpoint blockade could produce responses in a disease where single-agent PD-1 antibodies achieve response rates below 10 percent. This project will define the immune reprogramming caused by abemaciclib in estrogen receptor-positive mammary tumors, determine which effects are tumor-intrinsic and which are host-derived, and identify the schedule that maximizes combination benefit.

The central difficulty is that the drug acts on both sides of the interaction it is being asked to improve. The same kinases that drive tumor proliferation drive the clonal expansion of the effector lymphocytes on which checkpoint blockade depends, and continuous exposure produces lymphopenia in a substantial minority of treated patients. A schedule that maximizes tumor target coverage may therefore be the schedule that most suppresses the response being recruited. This is not a hypothetical concern: in our preliminary work, continuous dosing produced an effector to regulatory ratio roughly half that achieved on an intermittent schedule at matched cumulative dose.

Separating the two compartments pharmacologically is impossible, since a systemically administered inhibitor reaches both. We therefore use reciprocal chimeras in which the kinase is rendered catalytically inactive by knock-in in either the tumor or the host while remaining intact in the other. This design answers questions that no dosing experiment can: whether the increase in antigen presentation requires the drug to act on the tumor cell, and whether the shift in lymphocyte composition requires it to act on the lymphocyte. Both questions bear directly on schedule, because an effect that requires the drug to act on the tumor cell will persist through a dosing holiday if the arrest persists, whereas an effect on the lymphocyte will not.

We expect to deliver a time-resolved description of the immune landscape under abemaciclib exposure in three estrogen receptor-positive models, a compartment assignment for each major effect, and a schedule comparison with complete regression as the endpoint and lymphocyte dependence established by depletion. Because the drug is already given to large numbers of patients, a schedule result would be testable clinically without new chemistry. All cytometry, sequencing, and tumor growth data will be deposited at publication. The models, the cytometry panels, and the knock-in strains required are established and characterized in our laboratory, so the project proceeds directly to the experiments rather than to reagent development. Each aim is interpretable on its own, and together they specify a testable clinical regimen.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text:
The hypothesis is that abemaciclib produces two opposing immunologic effects whose balance depends on schedule: a tumor-intrinsic effect that increases visibility to lymphocytes, and a host-intrinsic effect that restrains lymphocyte proliferation. Continuous exposure maximizes both; intermittent exposure preserves the first while relieving the second during the intervals when effector expansion occurs. The aims characterize the effects, assign them to compartments, and test the schedule prediction directly. Testing this requires three things that existing work has not combined: a time-resolved description of what the drug does to the immune compartment, a way to assign each effect to the tumor or to the host, and a schedule comparison in which cumulative exposure is held constant. The aims below supply each in turn, in the same three models.

Aim 1 will characterize the immune landscape after 7, 21, and 42 days of abemaciclib in three estrogen receptor-positive syngeneic mammary models using 42-parameter mass cytometry and indexed droplet transcriptomic profiling of sorted CD45-positive populations. The three time points span initial arrest, established persistence, and the phase in which the microenvironment has been remodeled, and are chosen so that effects can be attributed to a phase rather than reported as an endpoint difference. Tumor-infiltrating and draining lymph node compartments are profiled in parallel, since effector expansion occurs in the node and its suppression there would not be visible in the tumor.

Aim 2 will separate tumor-intrinsic from host-intrinsic effects using CDK6 kinase-dead knock-in tumors in wild-type hosts and wild-type tumors in Cdk6 kinase-dead hosts, with readouts of MHC class I surface abundance, ERV-derived double-stranded RNA, and type III interferon transcription. Four combinations are compared, including both wild-type and both kinase-dead, which allows any interaction between the compartments to be estimated rather than assumed absent. Drug is administered to all four groups so that the genetic manipulation is superimposed on the pharmacologic one, isolating the compartment in which catalytic activity is required. A prespecified secondary analysis examines whether the effects assigned to each compartment are additive, since a substantial interaction would indicate that the drug's benefit depends on acting on both simultaneously.

Aim 3 will compare concurrent, sequential, and intermittent abemaciclib plus anti-PD-1 schedules, with complete regression rate as the primary endpoint and CD8 depletion used to establish dependence on cytotoxic lymphocytes. Cumulative abemaciclib dose is matched across schedules so that the comparison is of timing rather than of intensity. A prespecified secondary analysis relates complete regression rate to the effector to regulatory ratio measured at day 21 in a parallel cohort, which tests whether that ratio functions as an intermediate readout that could be measured in patients. Depletion is verified by flow cytometry in every animal, and the analysis is prespecified to exclude animals in which depletion did not reach the required threshold.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text:
Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer is immunologically cold, with low mutational burden and sparse lymphocytic infiltrate, and it has been largely excluded from the benefits of checkpoint blockade. Any intervention that converts this phenotype would apply to the majority of breast cancer patients. CDK4/6 inhibitors are already given to hundreds of thousands of women, so a schedule change rather than a new agent could deliver the effect. However, the same drugs cause neutropenia and lymphopenia, and continuous dosing may suppress the very effector populations that checkpoint blockade requires. Whether the immune benefit and the hematologic penalty can be separated by schedule is the central unanswered question, and it cannot be resolved in immunodeficient systems.

The magnitude of the opportunity follows from the size of the population rather than from the size of any single effect. Checkpoint blockade has transformed outcomes in tumors with high mutational burden and has done almost nothing in this subtype, which accounts for roughly two thirds of breast cancer. Converting even a modest fraction of these tumors into responders would affect more patients than most successful developments in immunologically hot diseases, and the conversion would be achieved with two agents that are already approved, already manufactured at scale, and already familiar to prescribers. The combination would also be testable in an academic setting rather than requiring an industry development program, which matters for a question that no sponsor has an obvious commercial reason to ask.

Schedule is an unusually attractive variable because it is free. Changing the dosing pattern of an approved drug requires no new chemistry, no new manufacturing, and no new toxicology, and the resulting regimen can be tested in an investigator-initiated trial. The field's default has been continuous administration, chosen for target coverage in an antiproliferative framework that predates any understanding of the immune effects. If the framework is wrong, the default is likely to be wrong too, and correcting it costs nothing but the experiment. The corresponding cost of getting it wrong is equally low in resources and high in opportunity, since trials conducted on the wrong schedule will produce negative results that are read as evidence against the combination rather than against the timing.

The negative possibility is equally worth establishing. If the lymphocyte-restraining effect dominates at every schedule, then combining this class with checkpoint blockade is unlikely to succeed regardless of timing, and the several trials currently pursuing that combination are unlikely to be informative. A clear demonstration of that would redirect effort toward combinations that do not share a target with the effector compartment, which is a useful result even though it is not the one we expect. It would also spare patients from enrollment on combinations built on a premise that the preclinical data do not support, which is a form of benefit that is rarely counted but is real.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text:
The kinase-dead knock-in reciprocal chimera design is the key methodologic advance: it allows the drug target to be disabled genetically in either compartment while leaving the other intact, which no pharmacologic experiment can achieve. Second, we profile at three time points spanning the transition from initial arrest to established persistence, capturing the inflammatory secretory program at the moment it appears rather than after it has remodeled the microenvironment. Third, we treat schedule as an experimental variable with three prespecified arms rather than defaulting to continuous concurrent dosing, which our pilot data suggest is the worst of the three because it maintains lymphopenia during the period when effector expansion is required.

The choice of a kinase-dead knock-in rather than a deletion is deliberate and matters for interpretation. Deleting the kinase removes both its catalytic and its scaffolding functions and also triggers compensation by the paralogue during development, so a deletion phenotype cannot be attributed to the activity that the drug inhibits. A point mutation that abolishes catalysis while preserving protein abundance and complex formation models the pharmacology far more closely, and it allows the genetic and pharmacologic manipulations to be superimposed in the same animal without confounding. It also permits the drug to be given to all groups, so that any difference between chimeras is attributable to the compartment in which catalytic inhibition is possible rather than to differences in exposure.

Time-resolved profiling addresses a specific interpretive trap. The microenvironment observed at day 42 is the product of six weeks of secretion, recruitment, and remodeling, and any measurement made there describes the accumulated consequence rather than the initiating event. Sampling at day 7, when arrest is established but recruitment has barely begun, allows the initiating changes to be separated from their downstream effects, and the day 21 sample captures the interval in which the secretory program is most active. The three-point design is the minimum that supports this decomposition. Profiling the draining lymph node at the same time points extends the decomposition in space as well as time, since suppression of effector expansion would be visible there before any change appeared in the tumor.

Treating schedule as a prespecified variable with matched cumulative dose is a small design choice with a large effect on what can be concluded. Comparisons in the literature typically differ in both timing and total exposure, so a difference cannot be attributed to either. Matching cumulative dose makes the comparison specifically about when the drug is present, which is the variable a clinician could change. The main limitation is that murine and human pharmacokinetics differ, so the optimal murine interval will not transfer numerically, and we therefore express results in terms of the fraction of each cycle spent above a target-engaging concentration.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text:
Syngeneic models include a Trp53-null estrogen receptor-positive line, an MMTV-driven line propagated with estrogen supplementation, and an organoid-derived transplantable line. Abemaciclib is dosed at 50 mg/kg daily or on a five-days-on two-days-off schedule. Anti-PD-1 clone RMP1-14 is given at 200 micrograms every 3 days. Mass cytometry panels are barcoded to permit 20 samples per acquisition. Double-stranded RNA is quantified by J2 antibody dot blot and by strand-specific sequencing of repeat elements. With ten mice per arm across nine arms we have 82 percent power to detect an increase in complete regression rate from 10 percent to 45 percent by Fisher exact test at a two-sided alpha of 0.05.

Estrogen receptor dependence of each model is verified before use by demonstrating growth inhibition on estrogen withdrawal and by confirming receptor protein and a transcriptional response to estradiol, since transplantable murine mammary lines drift readily toward receptor independence. All models are re-authenticated at each expansion and are used within a defined passage window. Estrogen supplementation is delivered by subcutaneous pellet with serum concentrations verified in a satellite group, because supraphysiologic estrogen has its own effects on myeloid populations and would confound the immune readouts if uncontrolled. Tumor growth rates in the absence of treatment are characterized for each model before any combination experiment, since models that grow rapidly leave too short an interval for an immune response to develop and would bias the schedule comparison toward the arm with the earliest exposure.

Cytometry data are analyzed with a prespecified gating hierarchy applied by an analyst blinded to arm, supplemented by unsupervised clustering on the same files so that populations not anticipated by the gating strategy can be recovered. Barcoding places all arms of a given experiment in a single acquisition, which removes machine drift as a source of between-arm difference. Transcriptomic profiling of sorted CD45-positive cells uses hashtag multiplexing with the same rationale. Complete regression rates are compared by Fisher exact test with prespecified pairwise contrasts among the three schedules, and the day 21 effector to regulatory ratio is related to regression by logistic regression across arms.

Contingencies have been planned for the three most likely difficulties. If none of the three models responds to anti-PD-1 even in combination, the models will be characterized for the absence of a required element, and a fourth model with a defined neoantigen will be introduced to establish whether the failure is one of antigen rather than of schedule. If the kinase-dead host shows a developmental hematopoietic phenotype that confounds the chimera experiments, bone marrow chimeras will be constructed to restrict the genotype to the hematopoietic compartment. If depletion is incomplete, animals below a prespecified threshold verified by flow cytometry are excluded before unblinding. Randomization is by cage after stratification on tumor volume, tumor measurement and all immune analyses are blinded to arm, and group sizes are fixed in advance with all attrition reported.
