title: Prevalence, Reproducibility, and Prognostic Significance of HER2-Low Expression in Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We evaluated 1,842 hormone receptor-positive, non-amplified breast cancers for HER2-low status, defined as an immunohistochemistry score of 1+ or of 2+ with negative in situ hybridization. HER2-low tumors comprised 58.4 percent of the cohort. Agreement among five pathologists for the distinction between a score of 0 and 1+ was moderate, with a Fleiss kappa of 0.61, whereas agreement for amplified versus non-amplified was excellent at 0.94. Quantitative immunofluorescence showed a continuous distribution of receptor abundance spanning 2.4 log units with no natural break at the 0 to 1+ boundary. After adjustment for stage, grade, and treatment, HER2-low status was not associated with recurrence-free survival, with a hazard ratio of 0.97 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.83 to 1.13, arguing against an intrinsic prognostic effect.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Immunohistochemistry for HER2 was designed and validated to identify tumors with gene amplification, a categorical property with a strong biological correlate. It was never intended to discriminate within the low range, and the assay is deliberately configured so that weak staining is uninformative. That configuration has become a problem because low-level expression now determines eligibility for trastuzumab deruxtecan, an agent whose activity extends well below the amplification threshold. Before the clinical implications can be interpreted, two questions must be answered: how reproducibly can pathologists make the required distinction, and does low-level expression carry independent prognostic information that would confound outcome comparisons. We addressed both in a large consecutive cohort with linked treatment and outcome data.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Consecutive tumors resected between 2008 and 2018 were retrieved and stained with the 4B5 antibody on a single automated platform. Five pathologists blinded to outcome independently scored a 600-tumor subset. Dual in situ hybridization was performed for all 2+ cases. Quantitative immunofluorescence used tyramide amplification with cell-line calibrators of known receptor number per cell, expressed as receptors per cell on a log scale. Patients had received adjuvant endocrine therapy, and 412 had subsequently received palbociclib or ribociclib for metastatic disease after endocrine resistance developed. Recurrence-free survival was modeled by Cox regression with stage, grade, nodal status, age, and systemic treatment as covariates. Interobserver agreement was summarized by Fleiss kappa with bootstrap confidence intervals.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 1,842 tumors, 1,076 were HER2-low and 766 scored 0. Reassignment between 0 and 1+ occurred for 21.4 percent of tumors when scored by a second pathologist. Quantitative immunofluorescence values overlapped substantially across the ordinal categories: the interquartile ranges for scores of 0 and 1+ overlapped by 38 percent. Median receptor abundance was 4,100 per cell for score 0, 11,800 for 1+, and 34,500 for 2+ non-amplified. HER2-low status showed no independent association with recurrence-free survival or with overall survival. Among the 412 patients treated for metastatic disease, time to progression on first-line endocrine therapy plus palbociclib or ribociclib did not differ by HER2-low status, at 22.4 versus 21.1 months.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: HER2-low is a category imposed on a continuum by an assay operating outside its validated range, and one in five tumors changes category between observers. Because the distinction now governs access to an effective drug, this is a practical problem rather than a semantic one. Our data argue that HER2-low status is not prognostic, which simplifies interpretation of trial results but also means that any observed benefit must be attributed to the treatment itself. Whether low-level expression functions as a genuine predictive biomarker for trastuzumab deruxtecan, or whether the drug is simply active irrespective of expression above some very low floor, cannot be resolved by retrospective analysis and requires prospective evaluation with a calibrated quantitative assay.

title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in HER2-Low, Hormone Receptor-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer After Endocrine Therapy: A Randomized Phase 3 Trial

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: In this open-label randomized phase 3 trial, NCT03734029, 557 patients with HER2-low, hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer whose disease had progressed on endocrine therapy combined with palbociclib, ribociclib, or abemaciclib were assigned 2:1 to trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks or to physician's choice chemotherapy. Median progression-free survival by blinded independent review was 10.1 months with the antibody-drug conjugate versus 5.4 months with chemotherapy, giving a hazard ratio of 0.51 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.40 to 0.64. Median overall survival was 23.9 versus 17.5 months, with a hazard ratio of 0.64. Objective response occurred in 52.6 versus 16.3 percent. Interstitial lung disease of any grade was reported in 12.1 percent, with grade 5 events in 0.8 percent, and grade 3 or higher neutropenia in 13.7 percent.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Classical HER2-directed therapy is ineffective in tumors without gene amplification because trastuzumab and pertuzumab depend on receptor signaling that low-expressing tumors do not use. An antibody-drug conjugate with a high drug-to-antibody ratio and a membrane-permeable topoisomerase I payload changes the requirement: the antibody serves as a delivery vehicle, and killing can extend to neighboring cells that express no antigen at all. A large consecutive-cohort analysis established that tumors scoring 1+ or 2+ without amplification comprise about 58 percent of hormone receptor-positive disease, that pathologist agreement at the 0 to 1+ boundary is only moderate, and that the category carries no independent prognostic weight. Those findings framed the eligibility criteria and the interpretation of the present trial.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients had received one or two prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease and had progressed on endocrine therapy given with palbociclib, ribociclib, or abemaciclib. HER2-low status was determined centrally on the most recent available specimen using the 4B5 antibody, with dual in situ hybridization for all 2+ cases. Randomization was stratified by number of prior chemotherapy lines, prior use of an inhibitor of PI3K, and central HER2 score. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in the full analysis set. Imaging was performed every 6 weeks for 24 weeks and every 12 weeks thereafter. Patients with treated, stable central nervous system metastases were eligible and a prespecified subgroup analysis evaluated intracranial outcomes. Pulmonary events were adjudicated by an independent committee.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median follow-up was 18.4 months. Progression-free survival favored the conjugate across all prespecified subgroups, including patients with an immunohistochemistry score of 1+ (hazard ratio 0.54) and those with a score of 2+ without amplification (hazard ratio 0.48). Among 68 patients with baseline brain metastases, median intracranial progression-free survival was 9.6 versus 4.1 months. Duration of response was 10.7 versus 6.8 months. Adjudicated interstitial lung disease occurred in 67 patients, with a median time to onset of 5.6 months; 4 events were fatal. Dose reduction was required in 24.1 percent of conjugate recipients. Quality-of-life scores measured by the EORTC QLQ-C30 global health scale declined more slowly in the conjugate arm, with a median time to deterioration of 7.6 versus 4.8 months.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These results establish an effective option in a population previously treated as HER2-negative and demonstrate that antigen density thresholds derived from trastuzumab biology do not apply to conjugates carrying membrane-permeable payloads. The intracranial results are notable given the molecular size of the agent and warrant dedicated study. Two limitations bear on interpretation. First, HER2-low was assigned by an ordinal assay whose reproducibility at the relevant boundary is moderate, so some patients scored 0 elsewhere would have been eligible here and vice versa. Second, no patients with a score of 0 were enrolled, so the trial cannot establish whether a threshold exists at all. Pulmonary events remain the principal safety concern and require protocolized surveillance.

title: Alpelisib plus Fulvestrant After Progression on CDK4/6 Inhibitors in PIK3CA-Mutant Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We conducted a multicenter single-arm phase 2 study, NCT03056755, of alpelisib 300 mg daily with fulvestrant 500 mg in 145 patients with PIK3CA-mutant, hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer whose disease had progressed on a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Median progression-free survival was 7.3 months with a 95 percent confidence interval of 5.6 to 8.9, and the objective response rate was 20.7 percent. Grade 3 or higher hyperglycemia occurred in 27.6 percent and was managed with metformin in most cases; 11.7 percent discontinued for this reason. PIK3CA status determined in circulating tumor DNA agreed with tissue in 82.1 percent of paired samples, and patients whose plasma mutation was detectable at baseline had a shorter progression-free survival than those with tissue-only detection, at 6.1 versus 10.4 months.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Progression on a CDK4/6 inhibitor is now the commonest clinical situation in hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer, and the optimal subsequent therapy is undefined. PI3K pathway activation is the most frequent tractable driver in this setting, and alpha-isoform inhibition combined with fulvestrant improves outcome in PIK3CA-mutant disease. However, the registration trial enrolled few patients with prior CDK4/6 exposure, so the effect size in the population that now dominates practice was unknown. Dense serial plasma sequencing during palbociclib with fulvestrant has shown that PIK3CA H1047R and E545K can emerge during treatment in patients whose baseline plasma was wild type, raising the possibility that the pathway becomes more important precisely at the point where these patients are treated.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients had documented PIK3CA mutation in tumor tissue or plasma and had progressed on any CDK4/6 inhibitor given with endocrine therapy. Alpelisib was started at 300 mg daily with prophylactic antihistamine and fasting glucose monitoring at baseline, week 1, week 2, and monthly thereafter. Metformin was started for fasting glucose above 160 mg/dL per a prespecified algorithm. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by investigator assessment. Plasma was collected at baseline and every 8 weeks and sequenced with a 74-gene panel to 3,000-fold deduplicated depth. Simon two-stage design required 12 responses among the first 60 patients to proceed. Concordance between tissue and plasma genotype was assessed with Cohen kappa.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median prior lines for metastatic disease was two and 89 percent had received palbociclib. Median duration of prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure was 13.2 months. Median progression-free survival was 7.3 months and median overall survival was 21.8 months. Response was more frequent in patients with a single PIK3CA hotspot than in those with two or more, at 24.5 versus 9.1 percent. Patients whose prior CDK4/6 inhibitor duration exceeded 12 months had longer progression-free survival at 9.1 versus 5.4 months. Baseline plasma sequencing identified co-occurring ESR1 mutations in 41 percent, which were not associated with outcome, and RB1 alterations in 4.8 percent, which were associated with a median progression-free survival of 3.1 months. Rash of grade 3 or higher occurred in 9.7 percent.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Alpha-isoform inhibition retains meaningful activity after CDK4/6 exposure, though the benefit is shorter than in the CDK4/6-naive registration population, and the difference is compatible with accumulated endocrine resistance rather than with cross-resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition specifically. Two management points follow. Hyperglycemia is anticipatable and, with a prespecified algorithm, led to discontinuation in fewer than one in eight patients, which is lower than in earlier reports using reactive management. Second, plasma genotyping is adequate for patient selection given 82 percent concordance, but a detectable plasma mutation also marks higher tumor burden and worse outcome, so it should not be read as an equivalent substitute for tissue when interpreting prognosis.

title: Elacestrant versus Standard Endocrine Therapy in ESR1-Mutant, CDK4/6 Inhibitor-Pretreated Advanced Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We randomized 478 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor to elacestrant, an oral selective estrogen receptor degrader, or to physician's choice endocrine therapy. In the prespecified ESR1-mutant population, defined by circulating tumor DNA at baseline and comprising 47.9 percent of participants, median progression-free survival was 3.8 versus 1.9 months, with a hazard ratio of 0.55 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.39 to 0.77. The 12-month progression-free rate was 26.8 versus 8.2 percent. In patients without detectable ESR1 mutation the hazard ratio was 0.86 and the confidence interval crossed unity. Benefit increased with the duration of prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure, supporting ESR1 mutation status as a predictive biomarker rather than a prognostic marker in this setting.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: After progression on endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, patients whose tumors carry ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations have few effective options, since further aromatase inhibition acts upstream of a receptor that no longer requires ligand. Oral selective estrogen receptor degraders were designed to bind and destabilize the mutant receptor while achieving exposures unattainable with intramuscular fulvestrant. Serial plasma studies during fulvestrant have shown that a confirmed twofold rise in mutant allele fraction precedes radiographic progression by roughly eleven weeks and that Y537S progressively dominates over D538G during treatment, indicating that these variants are under different selective pressure. That observation motivated our prespecified analysis of outcome by specific substitution rather than by mutation status alone.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Participants were randomized 1:1 to elacestrant 345 mg daily or to investigator's choice of fulvestrant, anastrozole, letrozole, or exemestane, stratified by ESR1 mutation status, prior fulvestrant, and visceral disease. ESR1 status was determined centrally from baseline plasma using a validated next-generation sequencing assay covering codons 310 to 547 with a limit of detection of 0.5 percent variant allele fraction. The primary endpoints were progression-free survival in the full population and in the ESR1-mutant population, tested hierarchically. Imaging occurred every 8 weeks. Plasma was recollected at week 8 and at progression. The trial is registered as NCT03778931. A prespecified exploratory analysis related outcome to the specific ESR1 substitution and to the number of coexisting substitutions.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median follow-up was 15.1 months. In the full population, median progression-free survival was 2.8 versus 1.9 months with a hazard ratio of 0.70. In the ESR1-mutant population the hazard ratio was 0.55. Among mutant patients, those with prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure of 12 months or longer had a median progression-free survival of 8.6 versus 1.9 months, whereas those with less than 6 months of prior exposure derived no measurable benefit. Patients carrying Y537S alone had a hazard ratio of 0.49; those carrying three or more distinct substitutions had a hazard ratio of 0.81. Grade 3 or higher nausea occurred in 2.5 percent. Week 8 plasma showed a decline in mutant allele fraction in 61 percent of elacestrant recipients versus 22 percent of controls.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These data support ESR1 mutation testing in plasma at the time of progression on endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, and support treatment selection on that basis. The strong dependence of benefit on the duration of prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure is the most clinically useful observation: patients who progressed quickly on their first-line combination have endocrine-independent disease and are unlikely to benefit from any receptor-directed agent, whereas those with prolonged prior benefit retain dependence on the receptor. The reduced effect in patients carrying three or more substitutions is consistent with several tumor populations escaping by independent routes, and suggests that a single receptor-directed agent will not be sufficient in that group.

title: Loss of SLC46A3 and HER2 Antigen Downmodulation Drive Acquired Resistance to Trastuzumab Deruxtecan

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We generated trastuzumab deruxtecan-resistant derivatives of four HER2-low and two amplified breast cancer models by continuous exposure over 26 weeks, and analyzed nine paired patient biopsies taken before treatment and at progression. Two dominant mechanisms emerged. Reduced surface HER2 abundance, without ERBB2 gene loss, occurred in five of six resistant derivatives and in six of nine patient pairs, with a median 3.8-fold decrease measured by quantitative immunofluorescence. Independently, loss of the lysosomal transporter SLC46A3 reduced intracellular payload accumulation by 71 percent without altering antibody binding or internalization. ABCC2 upregulation contributed a third route in two models. Single-cell RNA sequencing showed that antigen downmodulation reflected expansion of pre-existing low-expressing cells rather than uniform transcriptional suppression, indicating selection within a heterogeneous population.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Conjugates carrying membrane-permeable payloads have extended effective treatment to tumors expressing HER2 far below the amplification threshold. In a randomized phase 3 trial in HER2-low, hormone receptor-positive disease, trastuzumab deruxtecan improved median progression-free survival from 5.4 to 10.1 months against physician's choice chemotherapy, with an objective response rate above 50 percent. Nearly all of those responses eventually fail, and the mechanisms are unlikely to resemble those of the naked antibody, because the conjugate depends on a chain of events that the antibody does not: binding, internalization, lysosomal trafficking, linker cleavage, payload export into the cytosol, and topoisomerase I engagement. Each step is a potential point of failure and each implies a different subsequent therapy.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Resistant derivatives were generated by exposure to escalating trastuzumab deruxtecan from 0.1 to 5 micrograms per milliliter over 26 weeks, with parallel vehicle-passaged controls. Surface HER2 was measured by quantitative flow cytometry against calibration beads and by immunofluorescence with cell-line calibrators. Intracellular payload was quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry after 24-hour exposure. Antibody internalization was measured with a pH-sensitive conjugate. CRISPR knockout and complementary DNA rescue were performed for SLC46A3 and ABCC2. Nine paired patient biopsies came from a prospective progression-biopsy protocol. Single-cell libraries were prepared from parental and resistant populations at 5,000 cells each. Xenografts and organoids derived from two of the paired patients were used for combination testing.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median surface HER2 fell from 18,400 to 4,900 receptors per cell in resistant derivatives, and ERBB2 copy number was unchanged. Resistant cells regained sensitivity after 8 weeks of drug withdrawal, with surface HER2 returning to 79 percent of parental levels, indicating reversibility. SLC46A3 transcript was lost in two derivatives and in one patient pair; knockout of SLC46A3 in parental cells reproduced a 68 percent reduction in payload accumulation and a 4.9-fold shift in the half-maximal inhibitory concentration, and complementary DNA rescue restored both. ABCC2 inhibition with MK-571 partially restored sensitivity in the two upregulated models. In single-cell data, a HER2-low subpopulation representing 3.1 percent of parental cells accounted for 74 percent of the resistant population, and its transcriptional profile was already present before exposure.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Acquired failure of this conjugate is mostly a delivery problem rather than a target-signaling problem. Antigen downmodulation is reversible and reflects selection of pre-existing low-expressing cells, which implies that rechallenge after an interval off drug is rational and that re-measuring antigen abundance at progression is necessary. Transporter loss is a distinct and irreversible route that predicts failure of any conjugate using the same linker chemistry while sparing agents with cleavable linkers released extracellularly. The reversibility we observe helps explain why quantitative antigen measurement at a single archival time point performs poorly for patient selection, and argues for repeat sampling at each treatment decision rather than reliance on the diagnostic specimen.

title: Adjuvant Abemaciclib for High-Risk Node-Positive Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer: Five-Year Invasive Disease-Free Survival

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We report the prespecified five-year analysis of a randomized phase 3 trial, NCT03155997, in which 5,637 women with node-positive, high-risk hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer received standard adjuvant endocrine therapy with or without two years of abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily. Five-year invasive disease-free survival was 83.6 percent with the CDK4/6 inhibitor versus 76.0 percent without, giving a hazard ratio of 0.68 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.59 to 0.79 and a p value below 0.0001. Distant relapse-free survival was 85.1 versus 78.3 percent. The benefit persisted after treatment completion, with separation of the curves maintained through year five. Central nervous system recurrence as first site occurred in 1.4 versus 2.3 percent. Abemaciclib was stopped before 24 months by 18.5 percent of participants, most often because of diarrhea.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: CDK4/6 inhibitors transformed the management of advanced hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and their extension to the adjuvant setting rests on the premise that micrometastatic disease shares the dependence on the pathway that established metastases show. Functional profiling across estrogen receptor-positive cell lines and xenografts demonstrated that RB1-null models are uniformly insensitive to palbociclib but that RB1 loss explains only a minority of insensitive models, with an eleven-gene E2F transcriptional output score performing considerably better as a discriminator. Because RB1 alterations are rare in untreated primary tumors, that work implies that most early-stage tumors should retain pathway dependence, and it also suggests where an assay for adjuvant patient selection might eventually come from.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible women had four or more positive axillary nodes, or one to three nodes with either grade 3 histology, tumor size of 5 cm or greater, or Ki-67 of 20 percent or higher. Randomization was 1:1, stratified by prior chemotherapy, menopausal status, and region. Endocrine therapy was physician's choice for at least five years. The primary endpoint was invasive disease-free survival by STEEP criteria. Imaging was performed only for symptoms, consistent with standard adjuvant practice. Plasma for tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA testing was collected at baseline, 12, and 24 months in a 1,240-participant subset using a personalized 32-variant multiplex assay. Analyses used stratified Cox models with a prespecified interim analysis after 390 events. Early discontinuation was recorded with reason and month.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median follow-up was 63 months and 848 invasive disease-free survival events had occurred. The absolute benefit was 7.6 percentage points at five years. Benefit was consistent across nodal strata, with hazard ratios of 0.71 for one to three positive nodes and 0.66 for four or more. Among 1,240 participants with baseline plasma, detectable circulating tumor DNA was present in 8.9 percent and was associated with a five-year invasive disease-free survival of 41.2 percent versus 86.4 percent for undetectable, with a hazard ratio of 6.1. Abemaciclib reduced recurrence in both plasma strata. Grade 3 or higher diarrhea occurred in 7.8 percent and venous thromboembolism in 2.3 percent. Among those stopping early, 62 percent did so within the first six months.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Two years of abemaciclib produces a benefit that continues to widen after treatment ends, which is more consistent with elimination of residual disease in some patients than with simple suppression during exposure. The plasma data support that reading, since patients with detectable tumor DNA at baseline had markedly worse outcomes yet still benefited. The magnitude of early discontinuation remains the principal practical limitation: nearly one in five participants stopped before the planned 24 months, mostly in the first six months and mostly for gastrointestinal reasons, and this occurred in an academic trial population likely to be more closely supported than the community setting. Strategies that keep patients on drug during the first six months are therefore likely to matter as much as the drug itself.

title: Intracranial Activity and Cerebrospinal Fluid Penetration of Abemaciclib in Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer Brain Metastases

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We measured unbound drug concentrations in paired plasma, cerebrospinal fluid, and resected tissue from 43 patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer brain metastases receiving abemaciclib, and evaluated intracranial response in a separate cohort of 58 patients. The unbound cerebrospinal fluid to plasma concentration ratio was 0.96 for abemaciclib and 0.72 and 0.81 for its M2 and M20 metabolites, compared with 0.09 for palbociclib and 0.04 for ribociclib measured in the same protocol. Resected lesion concentrations exceeded plasma by 2.1-fold. Intracranial objective response occurred in 5.2 percent and intracranial clinical benefit at 24 weeks in 24.1 percent. In orthotopic intracranial xenografts, Abcb1 and Abcg2 knockout raised palbociclib brain exposure 11-fold but altered abemaciclib exposure by only 1.4-fold, identifying transporter avoidance as the pharmacokinetic basis of the difference.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Central nervous system progression is an increasing problem in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer as systemic control improves, and it is usually managed with radiotherapy on the assumption that systemic agents do not reach the site. That assumption is rarely tested with unbound concentrations, the only quantity relevant to target engagement. In the adjuvant setting, a large randomized trial of two years of abemaciclib reported that central nervous system recurrence as the first site occurred in 1.4 percent of treated women versus 2.3 percent of controls over five years, a difference that would be difficult to explain if the drug were excluded from the compartment. That observation motivated direct measurement in patients with established intracranial disease.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients undergoing clinically indicated craniotomy received a timed abemaciclib dose 4 to 8 hours before surgery. Plasma and cerebrospinal fluid were drawn at incision and resected tissue was snap-frozen within 4 minutes. Unbound fractions were determined by rapid equilibrium dialysis at 37 degrees against pooled matrix, and concentrations were measured by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with deuterated internal standards. The response cohort received abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily with fulvestrant and underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging every 8 weeks, assessed by RANO-BM criteria. Orthotopic tumors were established by stereotactic injection of 200,000 cells into the right striatum of wild-type, Abcb1a/b-null, and Abcg2-null mice. Comparisons of exposure ratios used log-transformed values and mixed-effects models.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median unbound plasma concentration was 41 nanomolar and median unbound cerebrospinal fluid concentration was 39 nanomolar. The combined unbound exposure of abemaciclib plus active metabolites in cerebrospinal fluid exceeded the concentration required for 50 percent target inhibition in every patient sampled. Intracranial responses were confirmed in 3 of 58 patients, and 14 had stable intracranial disease at 24 weeks. Median intracranial progression-free survival was 4.9 months. Patients whose lesions had previously received radiotherapy had similar drug concentrations to radiotherapy-naive lesions, arguing against barrier disruption as the explanation. In knockout mice, palbociclib brain-to-plasma ratio rose from 0.05 to 0.55 while abemaciclib rose from 0.71 to 0.99, confirming that abemaciclib is a weak transporter substrate.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Adequate unbound exposure is achieved but intracranial responses remain uncommon, so drug delivery is not the limiting factor for this agent in this compartment. Serial plasma work in the metastatic setting has shown that acquired RB1 events and CCNE1 gain arise under CDK4/6 inhibitor pressure, and patient-derived model work has shown that cyclin E1 elevation permits continued proliferation despite full target blockade; the resected lesions in our series were enriched for both alterations relative to published extracranial frequencies, which offers a more likely explanation for the low response rate than exclusion of the drug. If intracranial lesions carry distinct alterations, treating them by extrapolation from an extracranial biopsy will mis-assign therapy for the compartment that most limits survival.

title: Single-Cell and Spatial Profiling of Paired Biopsies Reveals an AP-1-High Quiescent State After CDK4/6 Inhibition

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We profiled 38 paired biopsies taken before treatment and at progression from patients receiving endocrine therapy with palbociclib or ribociclib, generating single-cell transcriptomes for 214,000 malignant cells and 960-plex spatial data for 26 sections. A transcriptional state defined by high JUN, JUNB, and FOSL1 expression, low MKI67, and retained estrogen receptor signaling expanded from 4.2 to 21.7 percent of malignant cells at progression. This AP-1-high state carried a senescence-associated secretory signature and elevated PI3K-AKT pathway output. A separate CCNE1-high population expanded in 9 of 38 patients and was largely non-overlapping with the AP-1-high state. Copy-number-based clonal reconstruction showed that AP-1-high cells were distributed across clonal lineages rather than confined to one, indicating a plastic state rather than a genetically fixed subclone underlying resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Genomic analyses explain fewer than half of the clinical failures on endocrine therapy with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, and the alterations they do recover, chiefly RB1 loss and CCNE1 gain, are found in a minority of patients. This leaves open the possibility that much of the residual explanation is transcriptional and reversible. Work in patient-derived xenografts and organoids established that palbociclib drives most cells into a persistent senescent state with an interleukin 6 and CXCL8 secretory program whose survival depends on BCL-xL, and that clearing that population with a selective senolytic roughly doubles the time to regrowth. Whether an equivalent population exists in treated patients, and how it relates to genetic subclones, has not been established.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Biopsies were collected on ice and dissociated within 30 minutes using a cold-active protease protocol. Single-cell libraries targeted 5,000 cells per sample at 50,000 reads per cell. Chromatin accessibility was profiled from cryopreserved nuclei for 22 samples. Spatial transcriptomics used a 960-plex imaging panel with nuclear-expansion segmentation, validated against nine-marker immunofluorescence. Copy number was inferred with a hidden Markov model over 10-megabase bins and benchmarked against matched exome data. State abundance changes were tested with a Dirichlet-multinomial mixed model to control compositional false positives. Distances from each malignant state to CD8-positive T cells and FAP-positive fibroblasts were computed on segmented spatial coordinates and compared with a permutation null preserving tissue geometry.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: The AP-1-high state expanded in 29 of 38 patients, with a median fold change of 4.6 and a Dirichlet-multinomial p value below 0.001. It showed reduced MKI67 and E2F target transcripts, elevated CDKN1A, and an eighteen-gene secretory signature score in the top decile. Chromatin data showed increased accessibility at AP-1 motifs with no change at estrogen response elements. Spatially, AP-1-high cells lay a median of 84 micrometers from the nearest CD8-positive T cell versus 31 micrometers for other malignant cells, and were enriched within 40 micrometers of FAP-positive fibroblasts. The CCNE1-high population showed the opposite profile, with high MKI67 and no secretory signature, and was confined to single clonal lineages in 7 of 9 patients.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Two distinct routes of escape coexist in these tumors. One is genetic, clonally restricted, proliferative, and CCNE1-associated; the other is transcriptional, distributed across clones, non-proliferative, and immunologically shielded. They demand different interventions, and averaging them is precisely what bulk sequencing does. The AP-1-high state closely resembles the persistent senescent population described in patient-derived models, where survival depended on BCL-xL and pharmacologic clearance delayed regrowth; our data suggest that population exists in patients, is spatially excluded from cytotoxic T cells, and is supported by adjacent fibroblasts. That combination suggests that clearing it may require both a senolytic and relief of immune exclusion.

title: Vepdegestrant, an Estrogen Receptor PROTAC, Overcomes ESR1 Mutations and Synergizes with Palbociclib

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Vepdegestrant is a heterobifunctional molecule that recruits cereblon to the estrogen receptor and eliminates it catalytically. We characterized its activity across knock-in cell lines carrying wild-type ESR1 or the Y537S, Y537N, D538G, and E380Q substitutions and across eight xenografts, six of them established from patients with prior palbociclib exposure. Half-maximal degradation concentration was 1.8 nanomolar for wild-type receptor and between 2.1 and 4.6 nanomolar across mutants, with maximum degradation exceeding 92 percent in all genotypes. Fulvestrant, the only approved selective estrogen receptor degrader, achieved 44 to 61 percent maximum removal in the same systems. GREB1 and TFF1 transcription were suppressed by more than 90 percent. Combination with palbociclib produced tumor regression in 6 of 8 xenografts versus stable disease with either agent alone, supporting targeted protein degradation as a strategy for endocrine resistance.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Every approved endocrine agent works by occupancy, so activity depends on continuous binding and is eroded by substitutions that reduce affinity or stabilize the agonist conformation. Degrader chemistry replaces occupancy with removal and is catalytic, meaning a single molecule can eliminate many copies of the target. A randomized trial of the oral selective estrogen receptor degrader elacestrant against physician's choice endocrine therapy in patients previously treated with endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor reported a hazard ratio of 0.55 in the ESR1-mutant population but showed that benefit was concentrated among patients with prolonged prior benefit and was absent in those carrying three or more distinct substitutions. That pattern suggests that deeper receptor removal, rather than better antagonism, is what the resistant population requires.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: ESR1 substitutions were introduced at the endogenous locus in MCF7 and T47D by CRISPR knock-in and validated by allele-specific sequencing. Receptor abundance was measured continuously using HiBiT-tagged endogenous alleles read every 15 minutes for 24 hours, with half-maximal degradation concentration and maximum degradation fitted from four-parameter curves. Ternary complex formation was measured by time-resolved fluorescence energy transfer and surface plasmon resonance. Cereblon dependence was tested by CRBN knockout and by competition with lenalidomide. Whole-proteome selectivity was assessed by tandem mass tag labeling with 8,500 proteins quantified. Xenografts were treated with vepdegestrant 30 mg/kg daily, fulvestrant 5 mg weekly, palbociclib 90 mg/kg daily, or combinations, with eight mice per arm and a 60-day observation period.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Receptor loss was detectable within 2 hours and maximal by 8 hours, and persisted for 48 hours after washout, whereas fulvestrant effects reversed within 12 hours. CRBN knockout abolished degradation entirely and lenalidomide competition shifted the concentration response by 46-fold, confirming ligase dependence. Proteome-wide analysis identified no off-target protein reduced by more than 30 percent at 100 nanomolar. In Y537S xenografts, vepdegestrant produced a mean best change in tumor volume of minus 34 percent versus plus 18 percent for fulvestrant. Adding palbociclib deepened this to minus 71 percent and extended time to a doubling of nadir volume from 29 to 68 days. In the six models from palbociclib-pretreated patients, the combination still produced regression in four, all of which retained RB1 protein.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Catalytic removal achieves a depth and duration of receptor loss that occupancy-based agents do not, and this advantage is largest in the mutant genotypes where affinity-based approaches are weakest. The persistence of effect after washout is pharmacologically important because it decouples the duration of target suppression from plasma exposure. The retention of activity in models derived from palbociclib-pretreated patients, conditional on retained RB1 protein, suggests a straightforward selection rule for clinical testing. Combination benefit was absent in the two RB1-deficient models, which is expected given that removal of the receptor cannot restore a downstream brake that is no longer present.

title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Palbociclib and Exposure-Response for Neutropenia in a Real-World Cohort

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We developed a population pharmacokinetic model for palbociclib using 3,140 plasma concentrations from 612 patients treated in routine practice, and related exposure to hematologic toxicity. A two-compartment model with first-order absorption and a lag time described the data, with apparent clearance of 63.4 liters per hour and apparent central volume of 2,180 liters. Body weight, albumin, and concomitant moderate CYP3A inhibitors were significant covariates, together explaining 34 percent of interindividual variability in clearance. Patients in the highest exposure quartile had an odds ratio of 2.91 for grade 3 or higher neutropenia relative to the lowest quartile, with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.78 to 4.76. CYP3A5 and ABCB1 genotypes did not improve the model. Dose interruption occurred at least once in 41.2 percent of patients.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Palbociclib is dosed at a fixed 125 mg daily on a three-weeks-on schedule irrespective of body size, organ function, or concomitant medication, yet exposure varies more than fivefold between individuals and neutropenia is the dominant reason for dose modification. Registration pharmacokinetic analyses were conducted in trial populations with narrow eligibility, and it is unclear whether their covariate models transfer to routine care, where hypoalbuminemia, polypharmacy, and reduced renal function are common. A five-year randomized adjuvant trial of a related CDK4/6 inhibitor reported that nearly one in five participants stopped the drug before the planned 24 months, mostly within the first six months, which underlines the practical importance of understanding what drives exposure and its hematologic consequence.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients receiving palbociclib for hormone receptor-positive advanced or early breast cancer contributed sparse sampling at routine visits, with two to nine samples each. Concentrations were measured by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with a lower limit of quantification of 0.5 nanograms per milliliter. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling used first-order conditional estimation with interaction. Covariates were screened by stepwise inclusion at p below 0.01 and backward elimination at p below 0.001. Model evaluation used prediction-corrected visual predictive checks and a bootstrap of 1,000 replicates. Individual area under the curve at steady state was derived from empirical Bayes estimates. CYP3A5 rs776746 and ABCB1 rs1045642 were determined from buffy coat DNA in 448 participants. Neutropenia was graded by CTCAE version 5.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median individual area under the curve at steady state was 1,970 nanogram-hours per milliliter with a range from 640 to 5,410. Apparent clearance decreased by 18 percent per 10 gram per liter fall in albumin and by 31 percent with concomitant moderate CYP3A inhibitors, most commonly fluconazole and diltiazem. Grade 3 or higher neutropenia occurred in 58.7 percent overall and in 74.1 percent of the highest exposure quartile. Median time to first dose interruption was 6.4 weeks. Neither CYP3A5 rs776746 nor ABCB1 rs1045642 was associated with clearance after adjustment, with p values of 0.41 and 0.28. Simulation indicated that a starting dose of 100 mg in patients with albumin below 35 grams per liter would reduce predicted grade 3 or higher neutropenia from 71 to 49 percent while keeping median exposure within the trial range.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Exposure to palbociclib in routine care varies more widely than in registration trials, and a substantial part of that variation is explained by two easily measured factors. The exposure-toxicity relationship is monotonic and steep enough that covariate-guided starting doses could plausibly reduce hematologic toxicity without compromising efficacy, although this requires prospective confirmation because the exposure-efficacy relationship in this disease is flat over the studied range. The absence of any pharmacogenetic contribution is itself useful, since it argues against pretreatment genotyping. These results speak to dose selection and supportive management rather than to mechanisms of disease escape, which lie outside the scope of the present analysis.

title: Palbociclib in CDK4-Amplified Dedifferentiated Liposarcoma: A Single-Arm Phase 2 Trial

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Dedifferentiated liposarcoma is characterized by amplification of the 12q13-15 region containing CDK4 and MDM2, making it a natural setting for CDK4/6 inhibition. We enrolled 61 patients with advanced, CDK4-amplified, RB1-intact dedifferentiated liposarcoma to receive palbociclib 125 mg daily on a three-weeks-on one-week-off schedule. The primary endpoint of progression-free survival at 12 weeks was met, with 57.4 percent of patients progression-free at that time point against a prespecified historical control of 40 percent. Median progression-free survival was 4.2 months and one confirmed partial response was observed. Grade 3 or higher neutropenia occurred in 34.4 percent and dose reduction was required in 21.3 percent. Retained RB1 protein by immunohistochemistry was required for eligibility and was confirmed centrally in all enrolled patients.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Amplification of CDK4 provides a direct genetic rationale for inhibiting the kinase, and dedifferentiated liposarcoma carries this amplification in more than 90 percent of cases. The rationale depends on an intact downstream brake: functional profiling across estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer lines and xenografts showed that RB1-null models are uniformly insensitive to palbociclib regardless of upstream genotype, and that an eleven-gene E2F transcriptional output score measured before drug exposure predicts sensitivity better than RB1 mutation status alone. We therefore restricted eligibility to tumors with retained RB1 protein and collected pretreatment tissue for transcriptional analysis, in order to test whether the same cell cycle logic derived from breast models transfers to a sarcoma driven by amplification of the drug target itself.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients had measurable, advanced dedifferentiated liposarcoma with centrally confirmed CDK4 amplification by fluorescence in situ hybridization and retained RB1 protein by immunohistochemistry. Palbociclib was given at 125 mg daily for 21 of every 28 days. Imaging was performed every 8 weeks by RECIST version 1.1. The primary endpoint was the proportion progression-free at 12 weeks, with a Simon two-stage design requiring 18 of 40 in the first stage. Pretreatment tumor RNA sequencing was performed in 52 patients and an eleven-gene E2F output score was computed. Complete blood counts were obtained on day 1 and day 15 of each cycle. Correlative analyses of the E2F score against progression-free survival were prespecified as exploratory.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median age was 63 years and median prior lines was one. Thirty-five patients were progression-free at 12 weeks. Median progression-free survival was 4.2 months with a 95 percent confidence interval of 3.1 to 6.0, and median overall survival was 19.4 months. One patient achieved a confirmed partial response lasting 14 months. Among 52 patients with transcriptional data, those in the lowest tertile of E2F output had a median progression-free survival of 7.8 months versus 3.0 months in the highest tertile, with a hazard ratio of 2.26. MDM2 copy number was not associated with outcome. Dose was held at least once in 44.3 percent of patients, most often on day 15 for neutrophil counts below 1.0 times ten to the ninth per liter.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Palbociclib produces disease stabilization rather than tumor shrinkage in CDK4-amplified liposarcoma, a pattern consistent with a cytostatic mechanism acting on the cell cycle. The association between pretreatment E2F output and outcome reproduces in a sarcoma what was originally described in breast models, suggesting that pathway output is a more general determinant of sensitivity than the amplification status of the target gene. Our trial does not address hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, where the drug is used with endocrine therapy and where the biology of escape involves receptor signaling that is absent here. Whether combined CDK4 and MDM2 inhibition improves on these results is being tested separately.

title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease: Incidence, Radiologic Phenotypes, and Outcomes of Protocolized Management

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We pooled individual patient data from 1,150 recipients of trastuzumab deruxtecan across six breast cancer trials to characterize drug-related interstitial lung disease. Adjudicated events of any grade occurred in 13.6 percent, with grade 5 events in 1.2 percent. Median time to onset was 5.6 months with a range of 0.6 to 32 months, and 28 percent of first events occurred after 12 months of exposure. Four radiologic phenotypes were identified: organizing pneumonia in 47 percent, non-specific interstitial pneumonia in 26 percent, hypersensitivity pattern in 17 percent, and acute interstitial pneumonia in 10 percent, the last accounting for all fatal cases. Baseline oxygen saturation below 95 percent, creatinine clearance below 60 milliliters per minute, and pre-existing lung disease were independently associated with risk. Protocolized corticosteroid management shortened median time to resolution from 61 to 34 days.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Pulmonary toxicity is the principal safety concern with this antibody-drug conjugate and is the main determinant of whether patients can remain on an otherwise highly effective treatment. In a randomized phase 3 trial in HER2-low, hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer, the agent improved median progression-free survival from 5.4 to 10.1 months against physician's choice chemotherapy, but interstitial lung disease of any grade was reported in 12.1 percent with fatal events in 0.8 percent, and this has shaped both prescribing and monitoring practice. What has been missing is a description of the syndrome itself: whether it is one entity or several, when it occurs, who is at risk, and whether early intervention alters its course.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Individual patient data were obtained from six trials with adjudication by a common independent committee. All available chest computed tomography images at the time of the first event were re-read centrally by two thoracic radiologists blinded to outcome, with a third for disagreement, and classified into four prespecified phenotypes. Risk factor analysis used multivariable logistic regression with prespecified candidate variables including age, region, baseline oxygen saturation, renal function, prior thoracic radiotherapy, pre-existing lung disease, and cumulative dose. Time to onset was analyzed with cumulative incidence functions treating death and progression as competing risks. Protocolized management, introduced partway through the enrollment period, specified corticosteroids at 0.5 to 1 milligram per kilogram for grade 1 events with weekly imaging.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 1,150 patients, 156 had adjudicated events. Cumulative incidence rose steeply during the first 12 months and continued to increase thereafter without plateau. Grade 1 events comprised 51 percent and resolved in 84 percent of cases; grade 2 or higher events resolved in 46 percent. The odds ratio for baseline oxygen saturation below 95 percent was 2.42 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.51 to 3.88, and for creatinine clearance below 60 milliliters per minute it was 1.87. Neither HER2-low status nor prior thoracic radiotherapy was associated with risk. Among patients rechallenged after a resolved grade 1 event, 34 percent experienced a second event, of which two were grade 3. Protocolized management was associated with a lower proportion progressing from grade 1 to grade 2 or higher, at 12 versus 27 percent.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Drug-related lung injury with this conjugate is not a single entity, and the acute interstitial pneumonia pattern that accounts for all fatalities is distinguishable radiologically from the far more common and largely reversible organizing pneumonia pattern. The absence of a plateau in cumulative incidence argues for indefinite rather than time-limited surveillance. The finding that renal impairment and low baseline saturation identify higher risk is actionable at the point of prescribing. Rechallenge after resolved low-grade events was feasible in two thirds of patients, which matters because discontinuation removes an effective agent. This analysis addresses safety and does not evaluate antitumor activity or the mechanisms by which tumors escape the drug.

title: Financial Hardship, Adherence, and Dose Interruption of Oral CDK4/6 Inhibitors in a Safety-Net Health System

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We studied 438 patients prescribed an oral CDK4/6 inhibitor for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in a large safety-net health system between 2019 and 2024, linking pharmacy refill records, prior authorization logs, and structured financial screening. Median medication possession ratio was 0.79, and 31.3 percent of patients fell below the conventional adherence threshold of 0.80. Median time from prescription to first dispense was 19 days, with 22 percent waiting more than 30 days. Out-of-pocket cost exceeding 100 dollars per month was associated with non-adherence, with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.41 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.56 to 3.72. Patients reporting high financial toxicity on the COST measure were more likely to have unplanned interruptions, and non-adherence was independently associated with shorter time to treatment discontinuation.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Oral targeted agents shift the burden of administration and cost onto patients, and the resulting variation in how much drug is actually taken is invisible in trial datasets where drug is supplied free and dispensing is centralized. In a randomized adjuvant trial of two years of abemaciclib, 18.5 percent of participants stopped before the planned duration, mostly within the first six months and mostly for gastrointestinal reasons, in a population with trial-level support. The equivalent figure in a safety-net setting, and the contribution of cost and access rather than symptoms, has not been described. We linked dispensing, authorization, and financial data to quantify both the extent of the problem and its determinants.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients were prescribed palbociclib, ribociclib, or abemaciclib in the metastatic or adjuvant setting. Medication possession ratio was computed as days supplied divided by days of intended therapy, censoring at clinical discontinuation, planned holds, and death. Prior authorization records provided submission, decision, and dispense dates. Financial toxicity was assessed with the 11-item COST measure at treatment initiation and at 6 months. Multivariable logistic regression modeled non-adherence with covariates for age, insurance type, primary language, distance to pharmacy, treatment setting, out-of-pocket cost, and prescribed agent. Time to discontinuation was modeled with Cox regression treating adherence as a time-varying covariate. Missing financial data were handled by multiple imputation with 20 datasets.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Insurance was Medicaid for 46 percent and uninsured with charity coverage for 14 percent. Median COST score was 19, indicating substantial financial toxicity. Prior authorization was required for 94 percent of prescriptions and initially denied for 21 percent, with a median of 2 appeals before approval. Non-adherence was more common among patients whose primary language was not English, with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.68, and among those living more than 20 miles from the dispensing pharmacy, at 1.54. Adherence below 0.80 was associated with a shorter time to discontinuation, with a hazard ratio of 1.93. Unplanned interruptions for symptoms, principally diarrhea and neutropenia, occurred in 39 percent and were not associated with cost measures.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A third of patients in this setting take substantially less of these drugs than prescribed, and the reasons are largely structural rather than clinical: authorization delay, cost sharing, language, and distance. These are addressable through pharmacy navigation and copayment assistance, and our data suggest where to concentrate such efforts. The dissociation between cost-related non-adherence and symptom-driven interruption is important, because the two require different remedies and are often conflated in observational reports. This study measures delivery of therapy rather than its biological effect, and it cannot speak to whether reduced exposure alters disease outcome, a question that would require linked outcome data and careful handling of confounding by indication.

title: Neoadjuvant Trastuzumab plus Pertuzumab with De-escalated Chemotherapy in HER2-Positive Early Breast Cancer: Pathologic Complete Response and Three-Year Event-Free Survival

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We randomized 428 women with stage II to III HER2-positive early breast cancer to neoadjuvant trastuzumab plus pertuzumab with either twelve weeks of paclitaxel alone or standard anthracycline-taxane chemotherapy, followed in both arms by adjuvant HER2-directed therapy to complete one year. Pathologic complete response in breast and axilla occurred in 62.1 percent with the de-escalated regimen and 58.4 percent with standard chemotherapy, meeting the prespecified non-inferiority margin. Three-year event-free survival was 94.2 versus 93.1 percent, with a hazard ratio of 0.88 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.47 to 1.65. Grade 3 or higher peripheral neuropathy occurred in 2.1 versus 8.9 percent and febrile neutropenia in 1.4 versus 9.7 percent. Left ventricular ejection fraction declines of 10 points or more occurred in 5.6 versus 11.2 percent.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Dual blockade with trastuzumab and pertuzumab produces high pathologic complete response rates in HER2-positive disease, and the marginal contribution of anthracyclines in that context has become questionable given their cardiac and leukemogenic risk. Any de-escalation strategy depends on accurate assignment of HER2 status. A consecutive-cohort study of 1,842 hormone receptor-positive, non-amplified tumors reported that agreement among five pathologists for distinguishing an immunohistochemistry score of 0 from 1+ was only moderate, whereas agreement for amplified versus non-amplified was excellent at a kappa of 0.94. That reassurance about the amplification boundary, rather than the low-expression boundary, is what makes eligibility for trials such as this one reliable, and we required central confirmation accordingly.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible women had centrally confirmed HER2 amplification by dual in situ hybridization and clinical stage II to III disease. Randomization was 1:1, stratified by hormone receptor status, nodal status, and tumor size. The de-escalated arm received paclitaxel 80 milligrams per square meter weekly for twelve weeks with trastuzumab and pertuzumab; the standard arm received doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide for four cycles followed by the same taxane and HER2-directed regimen. Surgery occurred three to six weeks after the last dose. The primary endpoint was pathologic complete response, with a non-inferiority margin of 12.5 percentage points. Event-free survival was a key secondary endpoint. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline and every three months during HER2-directed therapy.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median age was 51 years and 58 percent were hormone receptor-positive. Pathologic complete response was 62.1 percent versus 58.4 percent, giving a difference of 3.7 percentage points with a lower confidence bound of minus 5.6, within the non-inferiority margin. Among hormone receptor-negative participants, rates were 76.4 versus 71.0 percent; among hormone receptor-positive participants, 51.8 versus 49.5 percent. Three-year event-free survival was 94.2 versus 93.1 percent overall and 97.9 versus 97.4 percent among those achieving pathologic complete response. Treatment was completed as planned by 91 percent in the de-escalated arm and 79 percent in the standard arm. Two patients in the standard arm developed symptomatic heart failure; none did in the de-escalated arm.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Omitting anthracyclines did not reduce pathologic complete response or three-year event-free survival while substantially reducing neuropathy, febrile neutropenia, and cardiac decline. The population studied here is defined by gene amplification and is therefore distinct from tumors expressing HER2 at low levels without amplification, which do not benefit from trastuzumab and pertuzumab and which require conjugate-based approaches instead. Longer follow-up is required because late recurrence in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive disease continues beyond five years. These results address the composition of chemotherapy in amplified disease and should not be extrapolated to the selection or sequencing of agents in the non-amplified setting.

title: Germline CYP19A1 and ESR1 Variants and Aromatase Inhibitor-Induced Musculoskeletal Symptoms

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Aromatase inhibitor-induced musculoskeletal symptoms affect up to half of treated women and are the commonest reason for stopping adjuvant treatment early. We conducted a genome-wide association study of 1,204 postmenopausal women receiving adjuvant anastrozole or letrozole, with symptoms captured prospectively by the PROMIS pain interference scale and the BPI-SF. The strongest association was at CYP19A1 rs4646, with an odds ratio of 1.42 per minor allele and a p value of 3.1 times ten to the minus 6. A second signal at rs7158782 near TCL1A approached genome-wide significance. Common germline ESR1 variants, including rs2234693 and rs9340799, showed no association, with p values above 0.4. Circulating estrone sulfate concentrations at 6 months were lower in rs4646 minor allele carriers, providing a plausible mechanism for the increased toxicity.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Adjuvant aromatase inhibitors reduce recurrence but impose joint pain, stiffness, and muscle aching severe enough that a quarter of women stop within two years, forfeiting much of the benefit. Why some women are affected and others are not is largely unexplained by clinical factors. Germline variation in estrogen synthesis and signaling genes is a natural candidate. It is important to distinguish this question from the acquired somatic ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations that arise under estrogen deprivation in advanced disease; those are tumor-derived, appear only after prolonged exposure, and were shown in a 486-patient plasma study to predict inferior progression-free survival on a further aromatase inhibitor while leaving fulvestrant benefit intact. The inherited variants studied here are present from birth and relate to symptoms rather than to tumor behavior.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Participants were postmenopausal women starting adjuvant anastrozole or letrozole after definitive surgery for stage I to III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Symptoms were assessed at baseline, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. The primary phenotype was a 2-point or greater increase in PROMIS pain interference T-score sustained across two consecutive assessments. Genotyping used a 700,000-marker array with imputation to a 1000 Genomes reference, yielding 7.9 million variants at an imputation quality above 0.4 and minor allele frequency above 1 percent. Association testing used logistic regression adjusted for age, body mass index, prior taxane exposure, and the first five principal components. Estrone, estrone sulfate, and estradiol were measured by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry at baseline and 6 months.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: The sustained symptom phenotype occurred in 47.3 percent of participants, and 24.1 percent stopped treatment before two years. The rs4646 minor allele frequency was 0.34 and the association was consistent across both agents, with odds ratios of 1.39 for anastrozole and 1.46 for letrozole. Carriers had a median 6-month estrone sulfate concentration of 41 versus 63 picograms per milliliter. No signal was detected at ESR1, at CYP2A6, or at UGT2B17. Women reporting symptoms were more likely to stop treatment before two years, at 38.4 versus 11.2 percent. Baseline vitamin D level, prior taxane exposure, and body mass index were each independently associated with symptoms in the clinical model, which explained 6 percent of variance compared with 2 percent for the genetic model.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A common germline variant in the aromatase gene itself is associated with musculoskeletal toxicity and with lower residual estrogen concentrations, suggesting that the symptoms reflect the degree of estrogen suppression achieved rather than an idiosyncratic drug effect. If confirmed, this implies that women with the risk genotype might be better served by switching agents than by escalating analgesia. The absence of any ESR1 signal is worth emphasizing because inherited variation at that locus has often been proposed as a general modifier of endocrine treatment experience. The variance explained remains small, so genotype alone is not a basis for treatment selection, and the practical value lies in mechanism rather than prediction.
